Reference

Requirements for production operation

This page lists every requirement of the production pages (installation, publishing, security containment, compatibility, operations, performance, accessibility and author onboarding), one row each. The statement is the owner bullet word for word. Change the bullet first, then copy it here.

Id Statement Page Testable how
INS-001 --yes MUST NOT accept a grant with the risk level high, a new replaces entry, or a key that is not yet trusted. Only --grant <grant> accepts a high-risk grant and only --trust <key_id> trusts a key. Test: install a package with one high-risk grant and an unknown signing key using --yes, then assert that the install exits 1 with install.review-required and that ilium plugin list shows no new plugin. install-flag-matrix install a package with one high-risk grant and an unknown signing key using --yes, then assert that the install exits 1 with install.review-required and that ilium plugin list shows no new plugin.
INS-002 --grant <grant> MUST accept only the grant it names, and every other high-risk grant MUST still block the install. Test: install a package with grants a and b, both high risk, with --grant a, and assert that the install exits 1 and that the grant file is unchanged. install-flag-matrix install a package with grants a and b, both high risk, with --grant a, and assert that the install exits 1 and that the grant file is unchanged.
INS-003 --grant MUST be refused with usage.invalid-value and exit 2 when it names a grant that the package does not request. The refusal MUST happen before any file change (proposed, owner to confirm). Test: pass --grant missing for a package without that grant and assert exit 2 and an unchanged store. install-flag-matrix pass --grant missing for a package without that grant and assert exit 2 and an unchanged store.
INS-004 --trust <key_id> MUST be refused with usage.invalid-value and exit 2 when the value is not a key id of the form the trust list uses (proposed, owner to confirm). Test: pass --trust abc and assert exit 2. install-flag-matrix pass --trust abc and assert exit 2.
INS-005 --allow-unsigned MUST NOT trust any key. A package installed with --allow-unsigned MUST show the state of an unsigned package in ilium plugin list, and a later update MUST still need its own signature rule (proposed, owner to confirm). Test: install an unsigned package with --allow-unsigned, then assert that ilium plugin info <id> reports no trusted signer. install-flag-matrix install an unsigned package with --allow-unsigned, then assert that ilium plugin info <id> reports no trusted signer.
INS-006 --dry-run MUST NOT write any file under the plugin root, the store, the registry cache or the grant file. It MUST exit with the code that the real install would give. Test: run --dry-run on a package that would succeed and on one that would fail with package.hash-mismatch, and compare the file tree before and after each run. install-flag-matrix run --dry-run on a package that would succeed and on one that would fail with package.hash-mismatch, and compare the file tree before and after each run.
INS-007 --locked MUST fail with dependency.lock-mismatch and exit 1 when the package named by the lock file has a different hash, and MUST NOT contact a registry for resolution. Test: change one byte of the package in the registry mirror, run --locked, and assert exit 1 and no network request. install-flag-matrix change one byte of the package in the registry mirror, run --locked, and assert exit 1 and no network request.
INS-008 --locked combined with --channel MUST be refused with usage.conflicting-flags and exit 2 before any work starts (proposed, owner to confirm). A lock file already fixes the version, so a channel has no effect. install-flag-matrix Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
INS-009 --locked combined with a local file or an HTTPS URL MUST be refused with usage.conflicting-flags and exit 2 before any work starts (proposed, owner to confirm). The lock file names plugins by id and version, so it cannot pin a file. install-flag-matrix Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
INS-010 --from-bundle combined with --registry MUST be refused with usage.conflicting-flags and exit 2 before any work starts (proposed, owner to confirm). A bundle is the only source for that install, so a second source is ambiguous. install-flag-matrix Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
INS-011 --from-bundle MUST read the package and its signed metadata from the bundle directory and MUST NOT open any network connection. Test: block the network, run install --from-bundle ./bundle com.example.notes, and assert exit 0 when the bundle is complete. install-flag-matrix block the network, run install --from-bundle ./bundle com.example.notes, and assert exit 0 when the bundle is complete.
INS-012 --channel combined with a local file or an HTTPS URL MUST be refused with usage.conflicting-flags and exit 2 before any work starts (proposed, owner to confirm). A file has no channel, so the value would be ignored silently. install-flag-matrix Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
INS-013 --reinstall combined with --locked MUST reinstall the locked package and MUST still fail with dependency.lock-mismatch when its hash differs (proposed, owner to confirm). The flag rewrites the store only from the same package bytes. install-flag-matrix Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
INS-014 --unskip MUST clear the skip mark only for the version being installed. It MUST NOT clear the mark of another version. Test: roll back from 1.3.0 to 1.2.0 so that 1.3.0 is marked skip, then install 1.3.0 with --unskip and assert that the mark of 1.3.0 is cleared and that no other version changes. install-flag-matrix roll back from 1.3.0 to 1.2.0 so that 1.3.0 is marked skip, then install 1.3.0 with --unskip and assert that the mark of 1.3.0 is cleared and that no other version changes.
INS-015 --allow-downgrade MUST NOT clear a skip mark, because a downgrade installs a version by name and the mark only controls which version update offers (proposed, owner to confirm). install-flag-matrix Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
INS-016 --no-backup MUST be accepted only by an update that runs a data migration. On a fresh install it MUST be ignored with a warning record and the command MUST still exit 0 (proposed, owner to confirm). Test: install a new plugin with --no-backup and assert exit 0 and one warning record. install-flag-matrix install a new plugin with --no-backup and assert exit 0 and one warning record.
INS-017 A combination of flags that this page does not accept MUST be refused with usage.conflicting-flags and exit 2 before any file or network access (PKG-425). Test: pass each pair from the refusal rows of this page and assert exit 2 and an unchanged state. install-flag-matrix pass each pair from the refusal rows of this page and assert exit 2 and an unchanged state.
INS-101 The second install of the same file MUST NOT change any file. Test: hash the store and installed.json, run the command again, and compare. install-worked-examples hash the store and installed.json, run the command again, and compare.
INS-102 A search with --limit 0 or --limit 101 MUST fail with usage.invalid-value and exit 2 before any network request (PKG-824, proposed, owner to confirm). install-worked-examples Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
INS-103 ilium plugin info of a plugin that is yanked MUST show the field yanked in its plugin record when the source is a registry (PKG-437). Test: yank version 1.2.1, run info, and assert the field appears. install-worked-examples yank version 1.2.1, run info, and assert the field appears.
INS-104 install --locked MUST NOT write installed.json when dependency.lock-mismatch is raised. Test: change the lock file's hash for one plugin, run the command, and compare installed.json before and after. install-worked-examples change the lock file's hash for one plugin, run the command, and compare installed.json before and after.
INS-105 rollback of a plugin with no previous version MUST fail with install.no-previous and exit 5 (PKG-433). Test: first-install a plugin, run rollback, and assert exit 5 and no change in installed.json. install-worked-examples first-install a plugin, run rollback, and assert exit 5 and no change in installed.json.
INS-106 rollback MUST NOT delete the newer version from the store. The store keeps the files until the next committed update removes them (PKG-266). Test: roll back, then list the store folder and assert that 1.3.0 is still present. install-worked-examples roll back, then list the store folder and assert that 1.3.0 is still present.
INS-107 update --all MUST leave every plugin that succeeded at its new version after a failure of another plugin. Test: make one of two plugins fail its signature check, run update --all, and assert exit 1 and the new version of the other plugin. install-worked-examples make one of two plugins fail its signature check, run update --all, and assert exit 1 and the new version of the other plugin.
INS-108 install --from-bundle MUST fail with install.download-failed only when the bundle is incomplete, and MUST NOT try to fetch the missing file from the network (proposed, owner to confirm). Test: delete the package from a bundle, run the install with the network blocked, and assert exit 1 and no connection attempt. install-worked-examples delete the package from a bundle, run the install with the network blocked, and assert exit 1 and no connection attempt.
INS-109 A second install that fails with install.locked MUST leave installed.json and the store unchanged. Test: hold the lock in one process, run an install in another, and compare the files. install-worked-examples hold the lock in one process, run an install in another, and compare the files.
INS-110 uninstall without --purge MUST keep the plugin data folder unchanged. Test: write a file into the data folder, uninstall, reinstall the same version, and assert that the file is still there. install-worked-examples write a file into the data folder, uninstall, reinstall the same version, and assert that the file is still there.
PUB-001 The registry MUST keep a version in verifying until stages 1 to 8 and the policy check finish, and MUST NOT show the version in index.json before it reaches live or queued-review. Test: upload a package whose signature check is slow, and read index.json during the wait; the version is absent. publish-publisher-workflow upload a package whose signature check is slow, and read index.json during the wait; the version is absent.
PUB-002 A version that reaches rejected MUST NOT be stored as a published version, and its version number MUST remain free for a new upload. Proposed, owner to confirm: the rejection record names the stage and the code, and the publisher can read it with ilium plugin info <id>@<version>, which exits 5 for a version that never became live. publish-publisher-workflow Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-003 A live version MUST move to yanked only through a signed change to the metadata, and the transition MUST keep the blob, the version entry and its hash (PKG-443). Test: yank a version, then compare the blob hash in snapshot.json before and after; the hash is unchanged. publish-publisher-workflow yank a version, then compare the blob hash in snapshot.json before and after; the hash is unchanged.
PUB-004 publish MUST NOT print the token, and MUST NOT print the Authorization header in any error message. Test: publish with a wrong token and grep the output and the log for the token value; no match is found. publish-publisher-workflow publish with a wrong token and grep the output and the log for the token value; no match is found.
PUB-005 publish MUST exit with the code in the table above for each listed code, and the exit_code of its result record MUST equal the process exit code (PKG-423). Test: trigger each listed code against a test registry and compare the two values. publish-publisher-workflow trigger each listed code against a test registry and compare the two values.
PUB-006 After a registry.unreachable or a timeout on publish, the publisher MUST run ilium plugin info <id>@<version> before publishing again. If the registry returns the version with the same SHA-256 hash as the local package, the publish is complete and the publisher records the hash. If the version is absent, the publisher MAY publish again with the same file. Proposed, owner to confirm: the CLI does this check itself and reports the outcome as publish.already-complete with exit 0 when the hashes match, and registry.version-exists with exit 1 when they differ. publish-publisher-workflow Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-007 A publish with the same file whose hash differs from the hash of the live version of that id@version MUST exit 1 with registry.version-exists, and MUST NOT overwrite the live version (PKG-394). The fix is a new version number. publish-publisher-workflow Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-008 yank MUST require --reason <text> and MUST store the reason in the signed metadata, and the reason MUST appear to the user in ilium plugin info. Proposed, owner to confirm: the reason has at least 10 characters and at most 200 characters. publish-yank-deprecate-takedown Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-009 A yank whose reason starts with security: MUST be applied by clients with auto_update = install at the next safe point, as Registry reference requires. Test: yank a version with security: in the reason, then check that a client with auto_update = install moves to the next version without a user action, and that a client with auto_update = notify only shows the notice. publish-yank-deprecate-takedown yank a version with security: in the reason, then check that a client with auto_update = install moves to the next version without a user action, and that a client with auto_update = notify only shows the notice.
PUB-010 yank and unyank MUST NOT change the hash, the signature or the length of any blob. Test: compare the blob's snapshot.json entry before and after a yank and an unyank; the three values are equal. publish-yank-deprecate-takedown compare the blob's snapshot.json entry before and after a yank and an unyank; the three values are equal.
PUB-011 A security: yank MUST NOT be reversed by unyank while the reason is not withdrawn. Proposed, owner to confirm: unyank of a security yank requires the operator's confirmation, recorded in the transparency log (PKG-802). publish-yank-deprecate-takedown Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-012 deprecate MUST NOT change installed copies or block any install. It MUST show the message and the successor id when the successor is in the registry. Test: deprecate a plugin with a successor, install it, and check that the install succeeds and prints the message once. publish-yank-deprecate-takedown deprecate a plugin with a successor, install it, and check that the install succeeds and prints the message once.
PUB-013 unlist MUST remove the plugin from index.json and from search, and MUST keep plugins/<id>.json, every blob and the lock resolution, as PKG-398 requires. Test: unlist a plugin, then run ilium plugin update on an installed copy and check that the update still succeeds. publish-yank-deprecate-takedown unlist a plugin, then run ilium plugin update on an installed copy and check that the update still succeeds.
PUB-014 A takedown MUST record the reason, the time and the rule of Content policy that applies, in revocations.json and in the transparency log. The reason shown to users MUST be the text the operator publishes in policy.json, not a private note. publish-yank-deprecate-takedown Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-015 A takedown MUST NOT delete the signed version entry. It removes the blob and marks the entry as blocked, so the hash remains known and a client can explain why an installed copy is disabled. publish-yank-deprecate-takedown Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-016 After a takedown, every maintainer of the publisher id MUST receive a notice (SEC-723), and the notice MUST include the appeal address from policy.json. publish-yank-deprecate-takedown Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-017 A mirror MUST be synced at an interval of no more than half of the shortest expires lifetime of the metadata it serves. Proposed, owner to confirm: the timestamp document expires 24 hours after it is signed, so a mirror syncs at least every 12 hours. publish-mirror-runbook Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-018 A mirror operator MUST alert when the expires time of timestamp.json on the mirror is less than 6 hours away. Proposed, owner to confirm: the alert threshold is 6 hours. Test: stop the sync, wait until the threshold, and check that the alert fires before the expiry. publish-mirror-runbook stop the sync, wait until the threshold, and check that the alert fires before the expiry.
PUB-019 A sync MUST leave the previous files in place when it fails, and MUST replace each file atomically (PKG-439). A reader who reads the mirror during a sync MUST see either the old file or the new file, never a partial file. Test: kill a sync during a blob download, then check that every file in the folder still verifies. publish-mirror-runbook kill a sync during a blob download, then check that every file in the folder still verifies.
PUB-020 A mirror MUST NOT change any signed byte. Its files MUST be byte-identical to the source for a full mirror (PKG-408). Test: compare the SHA-256 of each file on the mirror with the source; they match. publish-mirror-runbook compare the SHA-256 of each file on the mirror with the source; they match.
PUB-021 A partial mirror MUST re-sign index.json and snapshot.json with its own keys and MUST publish its own root.json (PKG-409). Its operator MUST NOT reuse the source registry's root key. publish-mirror-runbook Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-022 A takedown (PKG-403) MUST be applied to a mirror within 6 hours of the source registry publishing it. Proposed, owner to confirm: a mirror operator who cannot meet this MUST remove the affected plugin from the mirror with --allow and sync again. publish-mirror-runbook Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-023 A mirror operator MUST NOT remove a blob from a full mirror on its own decision. Removal follows a takedown or a signed change from the source registry, so that the mirror keeps the source's signed state. publish-mirror-runbook Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-024 A full mirror's folder MUST have free space of at least twice the size of the source's current blobs, so that a sync can write a new file before it removes the old one. Proposed, owner to confirm: the factor of 2 is a safety margin, not a measured need. Test: fill the disk to the threshold, run a sync, and check that the sync fails cleanly and leaves the previous files valid (PUB-019). publish-mirror-runbook fill the disk to the threshold, run a sync, and check that the sync fails cleanly and leaves the previous files valid (PUB-019).
PUB-025 A mirror operator MUST NOT store a mirror on a disk that is also the root of the operator's own build cache. Proposed, owner to confirm: keep the mirror on its own filesystem, so that a full build cache cannot stop the sync. publish-mirror-runbook Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-026 The registry MUST serve every file of the table over HTTPS with the path of the table, and MUST NOT serve a metadata document under a different name than the one its role uses. Test: fetch each path with curl --fail; each one returns 200 and the expected signed.type value. publish-registry-operator-guide fetch each path with curl --fail; each one returns 200 and the expected signed.type value.
PUB-027 The timestamp document MUST expire 24 hours after it is signed, and the registry MUST re-sign it at least every 12 hours even when nothing changed. Proposed, owner to confirm: 24 hours is the timestamp lifetime. publish-registry-operator-guide Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-028 The snapshot document MUST expire no sooner than the timestamp document, and SHOULD expire 7 days after it is signed. Proposed, owner to confirm: 7 days. publish-registry-operator-guide Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-029 The root document MUST expire no sooner than 365 days after it is signed, and the operator MUST rotate it at least 30 days before its expiry. Test: read root.json, compute the time left, and fail the check when it is under 30 days. publish-registry-operator-guide read root.json, compute the time left, and fail the check when it is under 30 days.
PUB-030 The registry MUST expose the expiry times of timestamp.json and root.json to the operator as a machine-readable status, and the operator MUST receive an alert when either is less than 6 hours or 30 days away, as PUB-018 requires for mirrors. publish-registry-operator-guide Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-031 The registry MUST NOT log a publish token, an Authorization header or a second-factor code in any log line (PKG-392). Test: publish with a known token, then search the logs for that token; no match. publish-registry-operator-guide publish with a known token, then search the logs for that token; no match.
PUB-032 Every publisher id MUST have at least two maintainers, and every maintainer MUST have a second factor enrolled (SEC-723). A publisher id with one maintainer MUST show the warning No second maintainer on its registry page. publish-registry-operator-guide Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-033 A publish token MUST be issued to one publisher id and MUST expire 90 days after it is issued (PKG-968). The operator MUST run a report of tokens older than 90 days each month. Proposed, owner to confirm: the monthly report is the reminder; the token itself expires on its own. publish-registry-operator-guide Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-034 A token revocation MUST take effect within one hour of the publisher's request or of a leak report (PKG-970). Test: revoke a token, then publish with it within the hour; the publish is refused with registry.auth. publish-registry-operator-guide revoke a token, then publish with it within the hour; the publish is refused with registry.auth.
PUB-035 The registry MUST answer an upload that exceeds the size limit with registry.size before it stores any bytes of the body beyond the limit. Test: upload 301 MiB and check that the disk usage of the blob folder does not grow by more than the limit. publish-registry-operator-guide upload 301 MiB and check that the disk usage of the blob folder does not grow by more than the limit.
PUB-036 The registry MUST answer an over-limit publisher with registry.rate-limited and a Retry-After header. The header MUST be a whole number of seconds. publish-registry-operator-guide Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-037 A takedown MUST be approved by a second operator when the registry has more than one operator. Proposed, owner to confirm: the second approval is recorded in the transparency log with the first. publish-registry-operator-guide Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-038 The operator MUST answer an appeal within 14 days (PKG-404) and MUST record the decision and the reason in the transparency log. A reinstated version gets a new version number. publish-registry-operator-guide Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-039 When a signing key or a publish token leaks, the operator MUST follow Registry key compromise and MUST NOT wait for the publisher to act first. The first action is to revoke the key or the token, within the time of PUB-034. publish-registry-operator-guide Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-040 When a published version is found to carry malware, the operator MUST take it down under PKG-403 within 24 hours of the report. Proposed, owner to confirm: 24 hours is the target for a confirmed malware report. publish-registry-operator-guide Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
PUB-041 The operator MUST back up the blob folder and the metadata folder together, so that a restore has a snapshot.json that matches its files. Test: restore a backup to an empty host and run the client checks of Publisher workflow and version states against it; every hash matches. publish-registry-operator-guide restore a backup to an empty host and run the client checks of Publisher workflow and version states against it; every hash matches.
SCU-001 When two or more mechanisms apply to one plugin, the host MUST show the reason of the strongest one in this order: block, policy kill, admin kill, user disable. The host MUST keep the record of every other mechanism, and it MUST NOT clear any of them when the strongest one is lifted. Proposed, owner to confirm. Test: disable a plugin, kill it, run unkill, and assert that the plugin stays disabled and the row names the user disable. security-containment-states disable a plugin, kill it, run unkill, and assert that the plugin stays disabled and the row names the user disable.
SCU-002 ilium plugin kill <id> and ilium plugin unkill <id> for an id that is not installed MUST exit with code 5 and the text not found, and MUST NOT write any state or audit record. Test: run both against an unknown id and assert the exit code, the text and that ilium plugin audit shows no new line. security-containment-states run both against an unknown id and assert the exit code, the text and that ilium plugin audit shows no new line.
SCU-003 When no session is running, ilium plugin kill and ilium plugin unkill MUST exit with code 6 and MUST NOT change any stored state. Proposed, owner to confirm for the second half of the rule. Test: stop the session, run each command, and compare installed.json and the kill flag before and after. security-containment-states stop the session, run each command, and compare installed.json and the kill flag before and after.
SCU-004 ilium plugin kill MUST refuse to run without --reason <text>, and it MUST store the reason in the plugin.killed audit record. Proposed, owner to confirm. The refusal code is not yet named. Test: run kill without --reason and assert that no kill is recorded and the refusal is shown. security-containment-states run kill without --reason and assert that no kill is recorded and the refusal is shown.
SCU-005 The kill MUST survive a restart of the server and a restart of the operating system. Each start MUST refuse activation of the killed plugin until unkill runs. This extends HST-516, which covers only a server restart. Test: kill, restart the operating system of an isolated test VM, start Ilium, and assert the instance state is still disabled-by-admin. security-containment-states kill, restart the operating system of an isolated test VM, start Ilium, and assert the instance state is still disabled-by-admin.
SCU-006 ilium plugin unkill <id> on a plugin that is blocked MUST leave it blocked, and MUST show the block reason that is in force (trust.key-revoked or registry.takedown). Test: block a plugin by key revocation, kill it, unkill it, and assert that the state is disabled-blocked and the reason is shown. security-containment-states block a plugin by key revocation, kill it, unkill it, and assert that the state is disabled-blocked and the reason is shown.
SCU-007 While a policy kill lists a plugin id, ilium plugin unkill <id> MUST be refused with kill.policy-held and MUST leave the state unchanged. Proposed, owner to confirm. The operator lifts a policy kill by removing the entry and reloading the policy (LIF-302). Test: add a kill entry, kill and unkill through the CLI, and assert the refusal and an unchanged state. Then remove the entry and assert that the plugin is still refused until unkill. security-containment-states add a kill entry, kill and unkill through the CLI, and assert the refusal and an unchanged state. Then remove the entry and assert that the plugin is still refused until unkill.
SCU-008 An update that installs a new version of a killed plugin MUST NOT clear the kill. The kill is keyed by plugin id, so the user checks the new version and then runs unkill. Proposed, owner to confirm. Test: kill version A, install version B with ilium plugin update, and assert that activation is refused and the status still shows disabled-by-admin. security-containment-states kill version A, install version B with ilium plugin update, and assert that activation is refused and the status still shows disabled-by-admin.
SCU-009 ilium plugin uninstall <id> of a killed plugin MUST remove the kill flag with the plugin record, and MUST keep its plugin.killed audit records. Proposed, owner to confirm. A reinstall starts with no kill, as a fresh install does (SEC-119). Test: kill, uninstall, read the audit log, reinstall, and assert that the plugin is not killed and that the earlier plugin.killed record is still there. security-containment-states kill, uninstall, read the audit log, reinstall, and assert that the plugin is not killed and that the earlier plugin.killed record is still there.
SCU-010 A second ilium plugin kill on a killed plugin MUST write one more plugin.killed record with its own reason and time, and MUST keep the state disabled-by-admin. Proposed, owner to confirm. Test: kill twice with different reasons and assert two audit records and one state. security-containment-states kill twice with different reasons and assert two audit records and one state.
SCU-011 A registry takedown or key revocation that reaches a killed plugin MUST set the package state to disabled-blocked and MUST keep the kill flag set. The row MUST show the block reason. The kill flag stays so that a later unkill cannot restore activation of a blocked plugin, because the block is still in force. Proposed, owner to confirm. Test: kill a plugin, revoke its key as compromised, and assert that the row shows Blocked and that the state is disabled-blocked after unkill. security-containment-states kill a plugin, revoke its key as compromised, and assert that the row shows Blocked and that the state is disabled-blocked after unkill.
CMP-001 The host MUST run the checks of the decision order in the order of the table, and it MUST report the code of the first failing check only. compat-load-decision-table Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-002 A refusal MUST leave the package out of the store and MUST leave the installed version, if any, active. compat-load-decision-table Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-003 The host MUST refuse a package whose section version differs from its api value in any part, with manifest.api-version, before any code of the component loads. compat-load-decision-table Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-004 A host upgrade that refuses an installed plugin MUST NOT uninstall it, change its files, its grants, its settings or its stored data. compat-load-decision-table Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-005 An installed plugin refused after a host upgrade MUST load again, without any change to its files, when the host that accepts its api runs again. The rollback of the host is the way back; see Host upgrade runbook. compat-load-decision-table Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-006 A package whose api is inside the window of the host MUST load through the adapter of its minor, and it MUST behave as it did on the host that released that minor for every item the adapter maps. compat-load-decision-table Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-007 A package.api-unsupported message MUST name the lowest and the highest contract version of the current window. compat-load-decision-table Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-008 A package that fails at one step MUST NOT be partly installed: the store MUST hold no file of it after the refusal. compat-load-decision-table Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-009 Each refusal in the table above MUST have a line in the audit log that carries the code, the plugin id and the api value of the package. compat-load-decision-table Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-010 The removal minor MUST be stated in the marking release notes, together with the successor, so that an author can compute the window of every affected package from the notes alone. compat-deprecation-timeline Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-011 A package built for M + 1 that still uses an item removed at M + 2 MUST be refused at install with a code of the ABI refusal table, and the removal MUST NOT change the code of any other package. compat-deprecation-timeline Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-012 A graduation or removal of an unstable feature MUST be named in the release notes one minor before it takes effect, and the host MUST write a deprecated record for each plugin that still lists the feature in that minor. compat-deprecation-timeline Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-013 A removal MUST NOT happen on a patch release and MUST NOT change the behaviour of any item other than the removed one ([API-086]). compat-deprecation-timeline Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-014 A marking release note MUST contain the item name, the successor name, the removal minor and the packages it breaks, in that order, so that a reader can check the timeline without the source. compat-deprecation-timeline Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-015 Before a host upgrade, the operator MUST save the list and the status of every installed plugin, so that a refusal after the upgrade can be compared with the state before it. compat-host-upgrade-runbook Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-016 Triage MUST classify every refused plugin by its code before any other step, and it MUST leave each plugin's files, grants and data unchanged. compat-host-upgrade-runbook Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-017 A pin set during triage MUST be listed in the bulk report of step 4, and it MUST be removed with ilium plugin unpin <id> once a version that the host accepts is installed. compat-host-upgrade-runbook Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-018 A host rollback MUST NOT change installed plugin files, grants or stored settings, and a plugin refused after the upgrade MUST load again unchanged once the earlier host that accepts its api runs again ([ABI-078] of ABI major versions). compat-host-upgrade-runbook Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-019 A plugin rollback whose stored data version is higher than the target supports MUST be refused with migration.data-newer, and the operator MUST NOT force it through a restore without the audit export of step 1. compat-host-upgrade-runbook Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-020 The bulk report MUST contain one row per refused plugin, in one output, with the refusal code and the declared api value of each. compat-host-upgrade-runbook Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-021 A runbook run MUST leave the audit export of step 1 and the two ilium plugin list --json files in the operator's own folder, not in the plugin store. compat-host-upgrade-runbook Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
OPS-001 The host MUST write one diagnostics log file for each server lifetime. When the server starts, it MUST keep the five newest log files of the session and MUST delete the older ones. Test: start the server seven times in one session and count the files in the session folder: five remain, and they are the five newest by start time. ops-diagnostics-and-logs start the server seven times in one session and count the files in the session folder: five remain, and they are the five newest by start time.
OPS-002 File logging MUST be off by default. Turning it on or off MUST take effect without a restart of the server, and MUST NOT delete the files already written. Test: switch file logging on, write a line, switch it off, and assert that the file still exists and that no line is written after the switch. ops-diagnostics-and-logs switch file logging on, write a line, switch it off, and assert that the file still exists and that no line is written after the switch.
OPS-003 ilium plugin logs <id> MUST print the log of that plugin only, oldest entry first. --tail <n> MUST print the last n entries and nothing else. Test: write 50 entries for two plugins and assert that --tail 5 of one plugin prints exactly five lines, all of that plugin. ops-diagnostics-and-logs write 50 entries for two plugins and assert that --tail 5 of one plugin prints exactly five lines, all of that plugin.
OPS-004 When the log folder is outside the granted path /tmp/.ilium-<uid>/logs, the report MUST show log directory not readable: <path> and MUST list no log files. The operator MUST NOT widen the grant by hand in the plugin manifest or in the user's grant store to make the report work. Test: set ILIUM_DEBUG_LOG_DIR to a folder outside the grant, build the report, and assert the line and the empty file list. ops-diagnostics-and-logs set ILIUM_DEBUG_LOG_DIR to a folder outside the grant, build the report, and assert the line and the empty file list.
OPS-005 Ilium MUST NOT send a diagnostics report or a log file to any network address. The only action that moves them is the user's own copy, export or attach. Test: build a report and attach one log with the network disabled, and assert that no connection is opened. ops-diagnostics-and-logs build a report and attach one log with the network disabled, and assert that no connection is opened.
OPS-006 Before a log or a report is attached to an issue, the attach flow MUST show the file name, its size in bytes and the warning that logs hold prompts and replies. Test: open the attach flow for a 1.2 MiB log and assert the three items on screen. ops-diagnostics-and-logs open the attach flow for a 1.2 MiB log and assert the three items on screen.
OPS-007 An operator who copies a log for a support request MUST remove private text from the copy first, or send the support bundle of USR-335 instead, which counts the redactions. The host redacts secrets and paths outside the home folder (HST-129), but it does not detect names, so the copy MUST be reviewed by a person. Test: read a copy of a log that contains a name, and confirm that the review step removes it. ops-diagnostics-and-logs read a copy of a log that contains a name, and confirm that the review step removes it.
OPS-008 A diagnostics report section from one plugin MUST name the plugin that supplied it. A section that gets no reply within 2000 ms MUST appear as a warning line in the report, and the report MUST still be built from the other sections. Test: a section plugin that does not answer; assert the warning line and the other sections present. ops-diagnostics-and-logs a section plugin that does not answer; assert the warning line and the other sections present.
OPS-009 The report MUST be at most 262144 bytes in total, and each section MUST be at most 65536 bytes. A section that is larger MUST be cut to 65536 bytes and end with the line [section truncated], and the report MUST say which section was cut. Test: a section plugin that returns 70000 bytes; assert the cut and the marker. (Proposed, owner to confirm: the marker text.) ops-diagnostics-and-logs a section plugin that returns 70000 bytes; assert the cut and the marker. (Proposed, owner to confirm: the marker text.)
OPS-010 The default log threshold MUST be info. Entries at debug and trace MUST NOT appear in ilium plugin logs unless the threshold is raised for the plugin, and the threshold MUST return to info when the server restarts. Test: write one debug entry, read the log, raise the threshold, write again, and restart. ops-diagnostics-and-logs write one debug entry, read the log, raise the threshold, write again, and restart.
OPS-011 When an operator finds a secret in a log, the operator MUST disable the plugin with ilium plugin disable <id> as soon as the secret is found, MUST rotate the secret at its issuer, and MUST record the incident in the site's change record. Deleting the log line is not a rotation. Test: write a fixture secret, run the procedure, and assert that the plugin is disabled and that the secret no longer works at the fixture issuer. ops-diagnostics-and-logs write a fixture secret, run the procedure, and assert that the plugin is disabled and that the secret no longer works at the fixture issuer.
OPS-101 No plugin MUST send telemetry, and the host MUST NOT record a telemetry consent, until the user sets the consent in the plugin's settings page. A new install MUST start in the state not-asked, which means no telemetry. Test: install a fixture plugin that declares telemetry, and assert that no network connection is opened and that its consent state is not-asked. ops-telemetry-consent install a fixture plugin that declares telemetry, and assert that no network connection is opened and that its consent state is not-asked.
OPS-102 The telemetry consent of one plugin MUST have one of three states: not-asked (the default), granted and declined. A plugin that is removed and installed again MUST start in not-asked. (Proposed, owner to confirm: the three state names.) Test: grant, uninstall, install again, and read the state. ops-telemetry-consent grant, uninstall, install again, and read the state.
OPS-103 The consent MUST be stored in the consent store of the user, under the key telemetry of the plugin id, in the same file as the other consents (grants and consents). It MUST NOT be stored in the plugin's own data folder, so that a plugin cannot change it. (Proposed, owner to confirm: the key name telemetry.) Test: write a grant, read the file, and assert that the key exists in the store and not in the bucket. ops-telemetry-consent write a grant, read the file, and assert that the key exists in the store and not in the bucket.
OPS-104 Each change of the state MUST write one audit record of kind consent-given or consent-withdrawn ([SEC-222], reference-audit-log). The record MUST name the plugin id, the new state, the actor and the time. It MUST NOT contain any telemetry content. Test: change the state three times and assert three records in the audit chain with the stated fields. ops-telemetry-consent change the state three times and assert three records in the audit chain with the stated fields.
OPS-105 Withdrawing a consent MUST stop plugin telemetry at the next send after the change. The host MUST pass the new state to the plugin, and the plugin MUST NOT be able to read a stale value after the change. Data that the plugin already delivered before the withdrawal is outside the host's control and MUST be described as such in the plugin's own privacy text. Test: grant, send, withdraw, send again, and assert that the second send does not reach the fixture endpoint. ops-telemetry-consent grant, send, withdraw, send again, and assert that the second send does not reach the fixture endpoint.
OPS-106 An administrator policy MAY restrict telemetry, for example by turning off all plugin telemetry on a managed machine. An administrator policy MUST NOT set a consent to granted and MUST NOT read the consent records of a user ([USR-344]). Test: set the policy to block telemetry, then grant a consent, and assert that the send still does not happen; then check that the policy file holds no consent value. ops-telemetry-consent set the policy to block telemetry, then grant a consent, and assert that the send still does not happen; then check that the policy file holds no consent value.
OPS-107 Accepting the install review of a plugin MUST NOT set the telemetry consent, even when the review lists network grants. Test: accept a review with an http grant to the telemetry host and assert the state stays not-asked. ops-telemetry-consent accept a review with an http grant to the telemetry host and assert the state stays not-asked.
OPS-108 The consent state MUST be shown on the plugin's settings page and in ilium plugin grants <id>, with the words not asked, granted or declined. Test: read both views in each of the three states. ops-telemetry-consent read both views in each of the three states.
OPS-201 A monitoring script MUST treat every exit code other than 0, 1 and 2 as a failure of the monitoring, and MUST NOT treat it as a healthy result. Test: run the script with a missing ilium binary and assert that the alert shows a monitoring failure, not healthy. ops-crash-isolation-health-and-kill-switch run the script with a missing ilium binary and assert that the alert shows a monitoring failure, not healthy.
OPS-202 An operator MUST read the state of a plugin with ilium plugin status <id> before any action that changes it. A kill, disable or uninstall MUST NOT be the first step of a triage. Test: a fixture plugin in degraded state; the runbook steps must reach the status read before the kill command. ops-crash-isolation-health-and-kill-switch a fixture plugin in degraded state; the runbook steps must reach the status read before the kill command.
OPS-203 A kill MUST carry a reason. ilium plugin kill <plugin-id> --reason <text> MUST refuse an empty reason and MUST print the refusal code without stopping the plugin. Test: run the command with an empty reason and assert the refusal and that the plugin is still running. (Proposed, owner to confirm: the refusal code name.) ops-crash-isolation-health-and-kill-switch run the command with an empty reason and assert the refusal and that the plugin is still running. (Proposed, owner to confirm: the refusal code name.)
OPS-204 A killed plugin MUST stay killed across a server restart and across a reload of the policy file, until an explicit re-enable runs the grant review (SEC-458). A restart MUST NOT re-enable it, and a policy reload that does not list it MUST NOT re-enable it. (Proposed, owner to confirm: the policy-reload part, which extends HST-516.) Test: kill, restart the server, reload the policy, and assert the state disabled-by-admin after each step. ops-crash-isolation-health-and-kill-switch kill, restart the server, reload the policy, and assert the state disabled-by-admin after each step.
OPS-205 A kill MUST leave the crash records of the plugin in place. (Proposed, owner to confirm.) The kill switch MUST NOT delete the crash marks of the crash-loop guard ([LIF-294] clears them only after a stable start). Test: kill a plugin that has crash marks and assert that the marks and the records still exist after the kill. ops-crash-isolation-health-and-kill-switch kill a plugin that has crash marks and assert that the marks and the records still exist after the kill.
OPS-206 The kill switch MUST NOT be applied to an essential core plugin that the host protects ([LIF-030], [LIF-042]). The command MUST refuse it and name the reason. (Proposed, owner to confirm: the refusal wording and the refusal code.) Test: run the kill command against an essential core plugin and assert the refusal and that the plugin still runs. ops-crash-isolation-health-and-kill-switch run the kill command against an essential core plugin and assert the refusal and that the plugin still runs.
OPS-207 When a plugin is killed, every pending request of its instances MUST complete as cancelled within the times of HST-517, and the other plugins MUST keep their pending requests. Test: give a fixture plugin three pending requests, kill it, and count the outcomes. ops-crash-isolation-health-and-kill-switch give a fixture plugin three pending requests, kill it, and count the outcomes.
OPS-208 The operator MUST record each kill and each re-enable in the incident record of the site, with the actor, the reason and the time, in addition to the audit record of [SEC-458]. Test: read the incident record after one kill and one re-enable. ops-crash-isolation-health-and-kill-switch read the incident record after one kill and one re-enable.
OPS-209 After a crash or a kill, a call that was pending at the moment of the stop MUST NOT complete for the new activation, MUST NOT be replayed by the host, and MUST NOT be reported with the code cancelled, because only a clean shutdown produces that code. The host MUST NOT store pending calls durably to make this known. Test: give a fixture plugin one pending fs write, kill the server during the call, start the server, and assert that the new activation receives no completion for that call and that the file was not written a second time. (proposed, owner to confirm) host-upgrade-while-plugins-run give a fixture plugin one pending fs write, kill the server during the call, start the server, and assert that the new activation receives no completion for that call and that the file was not written a second time. (proposed, owner to confirm)
OPS-210 A plugin that makes a write MUST first store its intent in its own data storage under a key it chooses, with a unique idempotency key for that write, and MUST mark the intent as done only after the write returns ok. Test: write an intent, kill the server before the write returns, restart, and assert that the intent is still stored and not marked as done. (proposed, owner to confirm) host-upgrade-while-plugins-run write an intent, kill the server before the write returns, restart, and assert that the intent is still stored and not marked as done. (proposed, owner to confirm)
OPS-211 On each activation, a plugin MUST read every intent that is not marked as done, MUST check the target state that the write would have changed, and MUST repeat the write only when that check shows the write did not apply. A plugin MUST NOT repeat a write whose check shows that it applied. Test: leave one intent whose write applied before a kill, restart, and assert that the plugin repeats no write and marks the intent as done. (proposed, owner to confirm) host-upgrade-while-plugins-run leave one intent whose write applied before a kill, restart, and assert that the plugin repeats no write and marks the intent as done. (proposed, owner to confirm)
OPS-212 After every restore the administrator MUST run the four checks above for each restored plugin, in that order, and MUST NOT give users access to a plugin whose check shows failed, stopped-by-failure or a crash record written after the restore. Test: restore an archive of a fixture plugin whose activate traps, run the four checks, and assert that the plugin is listed as failed with a crash record and that the procedure stops there. (proposed, owner to confirm) guide-backup-and-restore restore an archive of a fixture plugin whose activate traps, run the four checks, and assert that the plugin is listed as failed with a crash record and that the procedure stops there. (proposed, owner to confirm)
OPS-213 Before a restore into a live data root, the administrator MUST create a new archive with ilium plugin backup and MUST keep that archive until the restored data has passed the checks of OPS-212. Test: run a restore into a live root and assert that a new archive exists, dated before the restore, and that the restore is refused while no archive exists. (proposed, owner to confirm) guide-backup-and-restore run a restore into a live root and assert that a new archive exists, dated before the restore, and that the restore is refused while no archive exists. (proposed, owner to confirm)
OPS-214 When a restored plugin fails the checks of OPS-212, the administrator MUST return the data to its pre-restore state by restoring the archive of OPS-213 with ilium plugin restore <file> --dry-run first and then --replace or --merge. --replace removes the plugins that the archive does not hold, so the administrator MUST use it only when no plugin was installed after the archive was made, and --merge keeps those plugins. The administrator MUST NOT run either command until the dry run shows the list of changes and the administrator has read it. A restore MUST run with the session server stopped, as HST-653 requires. Test: restore a broken archive, roll back with the pre-restore archive, and assert that the plugin's data matches the data before the first restore. (proposed, owner to confirm) guide-backup-and-restore restore a broken archive, roll back with the pre-restore archive, and assert that the plugin's data matches the data before the first restore. (proposed, owner to confirm)
OPS-215 During a rollback the administrator MUST NOT use --discard-data on any plugin, because it deletes data that a later check might need. Data is deleted only by a purge under HST-978, after an export. Test: run a rollback with a plugin whose data is newer than the archive and assert that no data was deleted and that the export step was required before any purge. (proposed, owner to confirm) guide-backup-and-restore run a rollback with a plugin whose data is newer than the archive and assert that no data was deleted and that the export step was required before any purge. (proposed, owner to confirm)
OPS-216 The administrator MUST write the result of the checks of OPS-212 in the restore drill log with the archive name, the date, and one line for each restored plugin with its state and its exit code. Test: read the drill log after a restore of two plugins and count one line for each plugin. (proposed, owner to confirm) guide-backup-and-restore read the drill log after a restore of two plugins and count one line for each plugin. (proposed, owner to confirm)
OPS-217 A unit that restarts the server on exit MUST NOT restart it after a clean stop with status 0. In systemd this is Restart=on-failure. In launchd it is KeepAlive with SuccessfulExit set to false. Test: stop the server with its own stop command, and assert that the service manager does not start it again within 30 s. (proposed, owner to confirm) guide-enterprise-deployment stop the server with its own stop command, and assert that the service manager does not start it again within 30 s. (proposed, owner to confirm)
OPS-218 A unit MUST wait at least 5 s before each restart after a failure, and MUST stop restarting when it has started the server 3 times within 300 s. In systemd this is RestartSec=5, StartLimitIntervalSec=300 and StartLimitBurst=3. In launchd the throttle interval MUST be at least 5 s. Test: make the server exit at start, and count the starts in 300 s: at most 3 in the window, then the unit stays failed. (proposed, owner to confirm) guide-enterprise-deployment make the server exit at start, and count the starts in 300 s: at most 3 in the window, then the unit stays failed. (proposed, owner to confirm)
OPS-219 A unit MUST NOT pass a safe-mode flag, such as --safe-mode, by default. The host chooses safe mode itself, by the guard of LIF-978 and LIF-979, and a unit that always starts in safe mode hides every plugin problem from the health checks. Test: read the unit file and assert that no safe-mode flag and no ILIUM_SAFE_MODE variable are set in it. (proposed, owner to confirm) guide-enterprise-deployment read the unit file and assert that no safe-mode flag and no ILIUM_SAFE_MODE variable are set in it. (proposed, owner to confirm)
OPS-220 The host does not send readiness or watchdog notifications to a service manager, so a unit MUST use the simple start type (Type=simple in systemd) and MUST NOT wait for a readiness signal. Readiness and health are read with ilium plugin health, whose exit codes are in Crash isolation, health checks and the kill switch (OPS-201). Test: read the unit file and assert the start type is simple, and that a monitoring check runs ilium plugin health and treats exit codes other than 0, 1 and 2 as a failure. (proposed, owner to confirm) guide-enterprise-deployment read the unit file and assert the start type is simple, and that a monitoring check runs ilium plugin health and treats exit codes other than 0, 1 and 2 as a failure. (proposed, owner to confirm)
OPS-221 The administrator MUST run ilium plugin audit --verify at least once a week (proposed, owner to confirm) from a scheduled job, and MUST also run it after each incident and before an audit export is sent outside the organisation. Test: schedule the job, let it run, and assert that its result is stored with the date of the run. guide-admin-failure-runbook schedule the job, let it run, and assert that its result is stored with the date of the run.
OPS-222 The administrator MUST record each verification result with the date, the exit code and the first finding, and MUST NOT close an incident while its last verification result is not ok, unless the only finding is torn-tail that the rule of OPS-223 explains. Test: run the verification on a clean log and on a log with one changed record, and assert that the records show exit 0 with ok and exit 3 with the first broken seq. guide-admin-failure-runbook run the verification on a clean log and on a log with one changed record, and assert that the records show exit 0 with ok and exit 3 with the first broken seq.
OPS-223 When the only finding is torn-tail (exit 0, as SEC-957 states), the administrator MUST record the byte offset, MUST check after the next server start that the partial bytes were moved to audit-torn-<seq> as SEC-956 requires, and MUST NOT treat the finding as a broken chain. Test: append half a JSON line to a copy of the log, run the verification, and assert exit 0 with the torn-tail line and its byte offset. guide-admin-failure-runbook append half a JSON line to a copy of the log, run the verification, and assert exit 0 with the torn-tail line and its byte offset.
OPS-224 When the verification reports broken, missing-file or reset-at, the administrator MUST follow the four incident steps above before any other action, MUST keep the copy of the folder unchanged, and MUST name the first finding in the incident record. Test: change one record in a copy of the audit folder, run the verification, and assert exit 3 with the first broken seq, and that the incident steps keep the copy unchanged. guide-admin-failure-runbook change one record in a copy of the audit folder, run the verification, and assert exit 3 with the first broken seq, and that the incident steps keep the copy unchanged.
OPS-225 When the verification reports unknown-schema with exit code 3, the administrator MUST upgrade the verifying host and run the check again before drawing any conclusion, because SEC-134 requires a newer schema to be read only by a verifier that knows it. Test: write a record with a schema value one higher than the verifier knows, run the verification, and assert exit 3 with unknown-schema and the seq of that record, and no finding of tampering. guide-admin-failure-runbook write a record with a schema value one higher than the verifier knows, run the verification, and assert exit 3 with unknown-schema and the seq of that record, and no finding of tampering.
PRF-001 An instance MUST reserve its effective memory_mib from the session memory pool when it activates, and MUST release that reservation when it deactivates. Test: with a pool of 1,024 MiB and eight instances of 128 MiB each, the ninth activation stays inactive with the reason host-capacity and no failure is counted; deactivating one of the eight lets the ninth start. perf-sizing-memory-and-cpu with a pool of 1,024 MiB and eight instances of 128 MiB each, the ninth activation stays inactive with the reason host-capacity and no failure is counted; deactivating one of the eight lets the ninth start.
PRF-002 When an instance grows its memory past its effective memory_mib, the host MUST trap the instance and count the trap as a failure. Test: a fixture that allocates 33 MiB with memory_mib 32 traps; the same fixture with memory_mib 64 passes. perf-sizing-memory-and-cpu a fixture that allocates 33 MiB with memory_mib 32 traps; the same fixture with memory_mib 64 passes.
PRF-003 A plugin SHOULD set memory_mib to no more than 1.5 times its measured peak on a release build, after the heaviest realistic input. Test: a fixture reports a peak of 20 MiB; the manifest value is at most 30 MiB. perf-sizing-memory-and-cpu a fixture reports a peak of 20 MiB; the manifest value is at most 30 MiB.
PRF-004 A plugin SHOULD keep its average spend on the execution bucket below 250 ms per second, measured over 60 seconds in normal use, which is half of the refill rate. (proposed, owner to confirm: the 250 ms figure is a proposal; the specification fixes only the bucket size and refill rate.) Test: a fixture that runs its normal event load for 60 seconds reports a spend under 15,000 ms in total. perf-sizing-memory-and-cpu a fixture that runs its normal event load for 60 seconds reports a spend under 15,000 ms in total.
PRF-005 A call that is refused with quota-exceeded MUST NOT be retried in a loop. The plugin MUST wait at least retry-after-ms before it submits again. Test: a submission loop against an empty bucket makes no more submissions in the refusal window than the retry-after-ms allows. perf-sizing-memory-and-cpu a submission loop against an empty bucket makes no more submissions in the refusal window than the retry-after-ms allows.
PRF-006 A plugin MUST NOT run a loop over its whole data set inside on-events or views.render. Work over a data set MUST run in a job. Test: a fixture with 100,000 items makes on-events return within 20 ms, and the same work appears as a running job in ilium plugin stats. perf-sizing-memory-and-cpu a fixture with 100,000 items makes on-events return within 20 ms, and the same work appears as a running job in ilium plugin stats.
PRF-010 A plugin MUST NOT retry a refused call sooner than its retry-after-ms value, and MUST NOT retry a quota-exceeded error that has no retry-after-ms without first freeing the resource it names. Test: a fixture with a rate rule of 1 call per 2 seconds makes 10 attempts in 5 seconds; the attempts after the first are spaced by at least retry-after-ms; a fixture that fills a storage bucket and retries put without freeing space makes no progress. perf-backpressure-and-retries a fixture with a rate rule of 1 call per 2 seconds makes 10 attempts in 5 seconds; the attempts after the first are spaced by at least retry-after-ms; a fixture that fills a storage bucket and retries put without freeing space makes no progress.
PRF-011 A plugin that retries a refused call MUST schedule the retry with a timer and MUST return from the handler before the delay ends. A plugin MUST NOT wait for a retry with a sleep or a loop inside a handler. Test: a handler that receives busy returns within 20 ms; the retry happens in a later batch after the timer fires. perf-backpressure-and-retries a handler that receives busy returns within 20 ms; the retry happens in a later batch after the timer fires.
PRF-012 A retry loop MUST stop after a bounded number of attempts. (proposed, owner to confirm: the default bound is 5 attempts, with the delay doubling from retry-after-ms and capped at 60 seconds.) Test: a call that is always refused makes exactly 5 attempts and then logs one warn line. perf-backpressure-and-retries a call that is always refused makes exactly 5 attempts and then logs one warn line.
PRF-013 A plugin SHOULD keep its own count of requests in flight below half of the pending_requests limit of its tier, so that a short burst does not reach busy. (proposed, owner to confirm: a half-of-limit rule is an author recommendation; the specification fixes the limit and the busy error only.) Test: a fixture that starts requests as fast as it can never has more than 32 in flight on T3. perf-backpressure-and-retries a fixture that starts requests as fast as it can never has more than 32 in flight on T3.
PRF-014 A plugin MUST handle an events-dropped event by re-reading the state it depends on, and MUST NOT assume that a count of drop-oldest events is complete. Test: a fixture that receives events-dropped with a count of 40 re-reads its state and its final output matches a fixture that received every event. perf-backpressure-and-retries a fixture that receives events-dropped with a count of 40 re-reads its state and its final output matches a fixture that received every event.
PRF-015 A handler MUST NOT keep work in the event queue by returning late. A plugin that needs more time than the batch deadline MUST start a job, as described in Moving slow work into a job. Test: a fixture that does 30 ms of work in on-events breaches the 20 ms deadline; the same work started as a job completes and the handler returns within 20 ms. perf-backpressure-and-retries a fixture that does 30 ms of work in on-events breaches the 20 ms deadline; the same work started as a job completes and the handler returns within 20 ms.
PRF-016 A plugin MUST NOT hold more than 256 KiB of unprocessed stream bytes for one stream, and MUST process or release each chunk before the next batch arrives. Test: a fixture with a slow job receives a 10 MiB stream and its buffered bytes never exceed 256 KiB; the stream completes. perf-backpressure-and-retries a fixture with a slow job receives a 10 MiB stream and its buffered bytes never exceed 256 KiB; the stream completes.
PRF-020 ilium plugin bench MUST label every timing record synthetic: true, and an author MUST NOT present a bench result as a session timing. Test: run bench on a fixture and assert that every timing record has synthetic set to true. perf-benchmark-workflow run bench on a fixture and assert that every timing record has synthetic set to true.
PRF-021 ilium plugin bench MUST exit 3 when any export's p99 is above its manifest deadline_ms, and MUST exit 0 when every export's p99 is within it. Test: a fixture whose handler sleeps 25 ms exits 3 for on-events, and a fixture that sleeps 5 ms exits 0. perf-benchmark-workflow a fixture whose handler sleeps 25 ms exits 3 for on-events, and a fixture that sleeps 5 ms exits 0.
PRF-022 A plugin author MUST NOT raise a deadline_ms in the manifest, or a limits value above the default of its tier, to make a bench or a CI gate pass unless the new value follows from a measured need. The commit that makes the change MUST name the measured numbers. Test: a review checklist item requires the measured numbers in the commit message. perf-benchmark-workflow a review checklist item requires the measured numbers in the commit message.
PRF-023 A handler SHOULD have a bench p99 of at most half its deadline, which is 10 ms for on-events and 5 ms for views.render at the defaults. (proposed, owner to confirm: the half-of-deadline target matches the warning colour in the handler budget meter in Performance, but no specification line requires it.) Test: a bench run of the reference fixture reports a p99 under 10 ms for on-events. perf-benchmark-workflow a bench run of the reference fixture reports a p99 under 10 ms for on-events.
PRF-024 A timing claim in a commit message, a changelog entry or a review SHOULD give the p99 of at least ten runs and the spread of those runs, so that a reader can tell a change from noise. Test: a review checklist item checks the message for both numbers. perf-benchmark-workflow a review checklist item checks the message for both numbers.
PRF-025 A baseline MUST be refreshed only in a commit of its own, after a release whose slower numbers were reviewed and accepted, or after a change of runner. Test: a commit that changes bench/baseline.json and any other file is refused by the review checklist. perf-benchmark-workflow a commit that changes bench/baseline.json and any other file is refused by the review checklist.
PRF-026 ilium plugin profile MUST print one timing record for each export call that ran during the profile, and MUST NOT change the call time of the plugin by more than 5 percent. This is the rule in Performance targets (DEV-850). Test: profile a fixture plugin with and without profiling and compare the call times. perf-benchmark-workflow profile a fixture plugin with and without profiling and compare the call times.
PRF-027 After a start or a resume, the host MUST deliver the overdue durable timers of one plugin side in due-time order, in batches of at most 32 durable-timer-fired events, and MUST keep the rest pending for a later batch. A pending timer MUST NOT be dropped or merged with another timer. (proposed, owner to confirm: the batch size of 32 is a default, not a value any specification line states today.) Test: a plugin with 100 overdue timers receives all 100 exactly once, in due-time order, in batches of at most 32. api-durable-timers a plugin with 100 overdue timers receives all 100 exactly once, in due-time order, in batches of at most 32.
PRF-028 The host MUST hold pending overdue fires outside the plugin event queue and MUST admit them into the queue only while the queue has room, so that one burst cannot overflow the never-dropped event queue and restart the plugin. Test: with an event queue of 64 entries and 256 overdue timers, the plugin is not restarted and all 256 fires arrive. api-durable-timers with an event queue of 64 entries and 256 overdue timers, the plugin is not restarted and all 256 fires arrive.
PRF-029 Each overdue fire MUST be charged to the ilium-execution bucket of its plugin side like any other event call. A fire MUST NOT be refused with quota-exceeded or busy; it waits in the pending list until the bucket is no longer empty. Test: with an empty bucket and 10 overdue fires, no fire is lost, and the first fire is delivered only after the balance is above 0 ms. api-durable-timers with an empty bucket and 10 overdue fires, no fire is lost, and the first fire is delivered only after the balance is above 0 ms.
PRF-030 A plugin that re-arms a repeating schedule SHOULD compute the next due time from the current time, not from the due time of the timer that fired, so that a long backlog does not produce a second burst of catch-up timers. Test: a plugin that re-arms an hourly schedule after a 10-hour outage arms one timer due within one hour of now, not ten. api-durable-timers a plugin that re-arms an hourly schedule after a 10-hour outage arms one timer due within one hour of now, not ten.
PRF-031 When more than 32 overdue fires are pending after a start, the host MUST write one entry to the host log for that start, with the number of pending fires and the largest late-by-millis, and MUST NOT write one entry per fire. Test: 100 overdue timers produce one log entry that states 100 pending fires and the largest lateness delivered. api-durable-timers 100 overdue timers produce one log entry that states 100 pending fires and the largest lateness delivered.
PRF-032 The host MUST give plugins one power value that says whether the machine is on battery or in a power-saving mode, and a plugin MUST NOT probe the operating system for that state itself. Test: a fake host that unplugs the machine changes the value that a plugin reads within 5 seconds, and the plugin reads the old value only before the change. reference-power-and-battery a fake host that unplugs the machine changes the value that a plugin reads within 5 seconds, and the plugin reads the old value only before the change.
PRF-033 While the machine is on battery or in a power-saving mode, the host MUST cap every scene frame rate at 30 fps, whatever the frame_rate_cap of the scene. (proposed, owner to confirm: the 30 fps figure is a default.) Test: a scene that asks for 60 fps runs at 30 fps on battery and at 60 fps on mains power. reference-power-and-battery a scene that asks for 60 fps runs at 30 fps on battery and at 60 fps on mains power.
PRF-034 While the machine is on battery or in a power-saving mode, the host MUST NOT fire an ordinary timer at an interval under 250 ms. (proposed, owner to confirm: the 250 ms floor is a default.) Test: a timer armed at 50 ms fires no more often than every 250 ms on battery and every 50 ms on mains power. reference-power-and-battery a timer armed at 50 ms fires no more often than every 250 ms on battery and every 50 ms on mains power.
PRF-035 The host MUST NOT scale deadlines, the execution bucket or its refill rate when the CPU throttles for heat or the operating system lowers the clock. A deadline missed during a throttle MUST count as an ordinary deadline breach. (proposed, owner to confirm: scaling deadlines was rejected because it would change the budgets of Performance budgets.) Test: a fixture that burns 25 ms of CPU in a handler is trapped at the 20 ms deadline, with or without a throttled core. reference-power-and-battery a fixture that burns 25 ms of CPU in a handler is trapped at the 20 ms deadline, with or without a throttled core.
PRF-036 A plugin SHOULD keep its idle wake-ups, counted as timer expiries and poll wake-ups with no event to handle, at 10 per second or fewer, so that a set of plugins stays inside the B24 budget on battery. Test: a plugin with one 250 ms timer and no events shows 4 or fewer wake-ups per second in a 60 second run. reference-power-and-battery a plugin with one 250 ms timer and no events shows 4 or fewer wake-ups per second in a 60 second run.
PRF-037 A find that matches more than 4,096 nodes MUST return the first 4,096 node ids in tree order and MUST NOT return an error. (proposed, owner to confirm: whether find truncates or refuses is an open decision; this is the default.) Test: a tree of 5,000 nodes and a find with every field unset returns 4,096 ids, and the first of them is the first node in tree order. perf-sizing-memory-and-cpu a tree of 5,000 nodes and a find with every field unset returns 4,096 ids, and the first of them is the first node in tree order.
PRF-038 When the pending tree-changed ids of one plugin side would exceed 4,096 entries, the host MUST deliver them in more than one tree-changed event, each holding at most 4,096 ids in first-seen order, and MUST NOT drop an id. (proposed, owner to confirm: the 4,096 figure is a default, and the rule replaces the single merged event for a larger burst.) Test: a burst that changes 10,000 nodes delivers ids in three events that cover each of the 10,000 ids exactly once. perf-sizing-memory-and-cpu a burst that changes 10,000 nodes delivers ids in three events that cover each of the 10,000 ids exactly once.
PRF-039 A plugin MUST NOT call find with every field unset, or walk children over the whole tree, inside on-events or views.render. It MUST build its index once, in an activation or a job, and update it from tree-changed and node-removed. Test: a fixture that walks a 5,000 node tree inside on-events is trapped at the 20 ms deadline, and the same fixture with an index built in a job is not. perf-sizing-memory-and-cpu a fixture that walks a 5,000 node tree inside on-events is trapped at the 20 ms deadline, and the same fixture with an index built in a job is not.
PRF-040 The benchmark for a 10,000 node tree MUST record, without a pass or fail threshold, the median and the 99th percentile of one children call on the root and of the delivery of one tree-changed event with 1,000 ids. Test: the benchmark result holds both numbers for the run, and the run does not fail on their values. perf-sizing-memory-and-cpu the benchmark result holds both numbers for the run, and the run does not fail on their values.
PRF-041 A plugin author MUST size the job pool of each side as the worst case of concurrent_jobs times memory_mib, and MUST state that worst case in MiB in the commit or review that changes either value. Test: a review checklist item for a change of concurrent_jobs or memory_mib requires the worst-case figure in MiB to appear in the commit message. perf-sizing-memory-and-cpu a review checklist item for a change of concurrent_jobs or memory_mib requires the worst-case figure in MiB to appear in the commit message.
PRF-042 A job start MUST be refused in the order of the five steps of this section: an oversized input first, then queueing, then busy when the queue is full, then host-capacity when the machine-wide ceiling has no room, and a runtime quota or timeout only once the job runs. (proposed, owner to confirm: the order of steps 2 to 4 is a default.) Test: with two live jobs and a full queue of 16 entries, a 17th start returns busy, and a start with an oversized input returns invalid-argument even while the queue is full. perf-sizing-memory-and-cpu with two live jobs and a full queue of 16 entries, a 17th start returns busy, and a start with an oversized input returns invalid-argument even while the queue is full.
PRF-043 A job start refused with host-capacity MUST NOT count as a failure, and the same start MUST succeed once memory or threads are released. Test: fill the machine-wide ceiling with running jobs, start one more and assert host-capacity with no failure counted; release one job and assert the same start succeeds. perf-sizing-memory-and-cpu fill the machine-wide ceiling with running jobs, start one more and assert host-capacity with no failure counted; release one job and assert the same start succeeds.
ACC-001 A plugin view MUST offer every action that a click can start through a focusable widget, so that Tab, Enter, Space or the arrow keys of that widget reach the same action. Test: for each action of the view, drive it with keys only and assert that the ui-action event arrives with the same key. a11y-keyboard-and-focus for each action of the view, drive it with keys only and assert that the ui-action event arrives with the same key.
ACC-002 A plugin SHOULD leave tab-index unset when the tree order already matches the reading order. A tab-index value MUST be set only where a control has to come before the order of the tree. Test: review the tree and list the nodes with a tab-index. a11y-keyboard-and-focus review the tree and list the nodes with a tab-index.
ACC-003 A plugin view MUST let Tab visit each focusable node exactly once in focus order, MUST return to the first node after the last, and MUST NOT contain an enabled focusable node that Tab does not reach. Test: send Tab once per focusable node and assert the sequence of keys. a11y-keyboard-and-focus send Tab once per focusable node and assert the sequence of keys.
ACC-004 A plugin MUST NOT make a hidden node the only way to an action. A disabled-reason MUST say why the control cannot be used. Test: focus each disabled node and assert that the reason appears in the screen text. a11y-keyboard-and-focus focus each disabled node and assert that the reason appears in the screen text.
