ACC-005 A plugin MUST NOT draw its own focus marker in the text of a view, such as a > or a reverse space in front of a row. Test: search the rendered rows for a focus glyph that the plugin wrote itself. a11y-keyboard-and-focus search the rendered rows for a focus glyph that the plugin wrote itself.
ACC-006 A plugin view MUST have exactly one focused widget at a time, and the focused widget MUST differ from the unfocused widgets by an attribute besides colour. Test: render the view at 48 columns, focus each widget in turn, and assert that one cell per step carries bold, underline or reverse. a11y-keyboard-and-focus render the view at 48 columns, focus each widget in turn, and assert that one cell per step carries bold, underline or reverse.
ACC-007 When a new tree removes the focused key, the host MUST place focus by the rule of the proposed decision on this page, which the owner must confirm before the rule is tested. A plugin MUST NOT depend on another node taking focus in that case. Test: rebuild the tree without the focused key and assert the focused key of the new tree. a11y-keyboard-and-focus rebuild the tree without the focused key and assert the focused key of the new tree.
ACC-008 A plugin that opens a dialog MUST test that Escape closes it and that focus returns to the widget that opened it. Test: open the dialog with a key, send Escape, and assert the focused key of the opener. a11y-keyboard-and-focus open the dialog with a key, send Escape, and assert the focused key of the opener.
ACC-009 A plugin MUST NOT bind Tab, Shift+Tab or Escape to a command, a keybinding or a key capture of its own. The host keeps these keys for focus and for closing. Test: review the keybindings of the manifest and the key captures of the view. a11y-keyboard-and-focus review the keybindings of the manifest and the key captures of the view.
ACC-010 A control that needs a drag, such as a draggable row or a drop-target, MUST have an action that does the same thing from the keyboard. Test: find the drop action of the view and drive it with keys only. a11y-keyboard-and-focus find the drop action of the view and drive it with keys only.
ACC-011 A plugin MUST NOT assume that a focus request moves focus to a view the user has not opened. When the user must act in that view, the plugin MUST also say so in the text of the view. Test: send a focus request to a view that was never focused and assert that focus is unchanged and the text still gives the instruction. a11y-keyboard-and-focus send a focus request to a view that was never focused and assert that focus is unchanged and the text still gives the instruction.
ACC-012 A plugin MUST give every focusable widget a label that names its action. The label MUST NOT contain the value, a state word or a role word that the host prints itself. Test: render the view in screen reader mode and assert that each line has the role word once. a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text render the view in screen reader mode and assert that each line has the role word once.
ACC-013 A plugin MUST NOT put meaning in a decorative glyph or an emoji inside a label. The meaning MUST be a word. Test: scan the labels of the view for characters outside letters, digits, spaces and punctuation, and assert that each one carries no meaning that the words do not give. a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text scan the labels of the view for characters outside letters, digits, spaces and punctuation, and assert that each one carries no meaning that the words do not give.
ACC-014 A plugin MUST put a status change in the words of the row that shows it, not only in a colour, a glyph or a moving frame. Test: change the status in the fake host, render the view, and assert that the row text holds the new state word. a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text change the status in the fake host, render the view, and assert that the row text holds the new state word.
ACC-015 A plugin MUST NOT rely on the screen reader to announce a text change in its view. A change that needs the user's attention MUST also raise a toast or a desktop notice with a persistent text twin (CAP-883). Test: review the change path of the view for an event that needs attention and check that it has the twin. a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text review the change path of the view for an event that needs attention and check that it has the twin.
ACC-016 A plugin that ships translations MUST build each accessible label from a message id of its own catalogue, and MUST NOT join two translated pieces into one label. Test: search the source for a label built with +, a format string with two translated parts, or a string concatenation. a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text search the source for a label built with +, a format string with two translated parts, or a string concatenation.
ACC-017 A plugin MUST NOT write a role word, such as button or toggle, into a label or a value. Test: render the view in screen reader mode and assert that no line holds the role word twice. a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text render the view in screen reader mode and assert that no line holds the role word twice.
ACC-018 A plugin MUST keep every label of its focusable widgets whole at 48 columns in the pseudo-locale en-XA with screen reader mode on. A label that is cut with … is a failure. Test: render the view with en-XA and screen_reader set in the test host, and assert that each linear line ends with its full label. a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text render the view with en-XA and screen_reader set in the test host, and assert that each linear line ends with its full label.
ACC-019 A plugin MUST keep a disabled-reason short enough to be read in one line at 48 columns, and MUST give the reason in words, not as a symbol. Test: render each disabled widget at 48 columns and assert that the reason is complete. a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text render each disabled widget at 48 columns and assert that the reason is complete.
ACC-020 A plugin MUST NOT show a message id, a key of a setting or a catalogue key in any label or value of a view, in any language. Test: search the rendered screen text in each shipped language for a dotted identifier that the plugin defines. a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text search the rendered screen text in each shipped language for a dotted identifier that the plugin defines.
ACC-021 A plugin MUST keep the same focusable widgets, with the same labels, in screen reader mode and in the normal view. A change of the mode MUST NOT remove a control or change its action. Test: render the view with the setting off and on, and assert the same set of keys. a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text render the view with the setting off and on, and assert the same set of keys.
ACC-022 A plugin test SHOULD check the linear output of each view once per release, with the screen reader setting on, and SHOULD compare its line order with the focus order of Keyboard operation and focus. Test: the test host reads the screen text and the focus order, and the assert compares both. a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text the test host reads the screen text and the focus order, and the assert compares both.
ONB-001 plugin new MUST create the common files listed in Project templates and the source files of the chosen template, and nothing else outside <dir>. authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-002 The publisher of a new project MUST be the operating system user name unless --publisher is given, and the display name MUST be the last label of the id unless --name is given. authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-003 The author MUST NOT edit files under dist/ by hand. build MUST be the only writer of dist/<side>.wasm and dist/build.json ([DEV-050], [DEV-051]), and test --coverage MUST write its output under .ilium/coverage/. authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-004 A fresh project MUST pass the four commands above with exit code 0 and no warning, in that order. The template guarantees this state ([DEV-045]). If a fresh project fails one of these commands, the author SHOULD treat it as a template or toolchain problem and report it, rather than edit the template files (proposed, owner to confirm). authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-005 test on a project with no built component for its side MUST fail with test.component-missing and exit with 1. The author MUST run build and rerun test. authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-006 A project with only Cargo.toml MUST build as Rust, and a project with only package.json MUST build as TypeScript. A project with both files MUST fail with toolchain.language-ambiguous, and a project with neither MUST fail with toolchain.language-unknown ([DEV-002]). The author MUST keep one language per project. authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-007 When a toolchain is missing, build MUST stop with a toolchain.* code and exit with 4 ([DEV-012], [DEV-055]). The author installs the named tool and reruns the command. Running doctor lists every missing item with status fail and also exits with 4. authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-008 check and lint MUST run without a network connection. check --print-schema MUST also run offline and print the manifest schema ([DEV-070], [DEV-075]). authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-009 dev MUST start a rebuild 300 ms after the last file change, and MUST ignore changes under dist/, target/, node_modules/, .ilium/, .git/ and the paths in .gitignore ([DEV-185]). authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-010 On a successful rebuild, dev MUST reload the server side first and then each attached client side. Each reload MUST print one reload record. A failed rebuild MUST print the compiler errors, keep the running instance, and send no deactivate ([DEV-187]). The author fixes the error and saves again; no restart is needed. authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-011 The development copy MUST be installed as tier T3 with the dev badge and with a data folder of its own. A real install of the same id MUST not share that data folder ([DEV-181]). If a real install of the id is already present, dev MUST fail with dev.id-installed and exit with 1, unless --replace-installed is given ([DEV-183]). authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-012 dev MUST build with debug information by default, so that a trap names file:line. --release MUST omit it ([DEV-182]). authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-013 Ctrl+C in dev MUST deactivate the plugin with reason disabled, uninstall the development copy, keep its data folder unless --purge-on-exit is given, and exit with 130 ([DEV-189]). authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-014 Restore bytes above 1 MiB MUST be dropped on reload, and the reload record MUST show restore_dropped true with restored_bytes 0 ([DEV-188]). An author who sees this MUST treat the reload as having lost its restore state and MUST NOT rely on that state surviving a reload (proposed, owner to confirm: the page does not yet name the storage API an author should use for large state). authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-015 A fixture with no expectation file MUST pass and print the warning test.no-expectation. The author SHOULD add an expectation for every fixture before the first CI run (proposed, owner to confirm: the warning is advisory today, and this page sets the team expectation, not a rule of the host). authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-016 test MUST exit with 0 when every case passes, 3 when a case fails or traps, and 1 when a fixture cannot be read ([DEV-087]). A mismatch MUST print a diff record. authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-017 A package with two sides MUST be given --side for test, or the command fails with usage.missing-argument ([DEV-085]). A one-side project needs no flag. authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-018 test --update MUST rewrite only the expectation and golden files that differ and MUST print one test.updated warning for each file rewritten ([DEV-086]). The author reads the diff in version control before committing the rewrite. authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-019 test MUST NOT run the project's own unit tests. Those run with cargo test or bun test in native mode, and test --coverage is the only form of test that starts them ([DEV-089]). authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-020 An author who sees exit code 3 from test MUST read the first diff or trap record before changing the code, and MUST NOT update the expectation file to hide a trap ([DEV-084]). test --update is for an intended change of output only. authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
ONB-021 An author who sees a trap MUST use the file:line of the trap and the reason in its record. For a trap in a release build, which has no debug information, the author MUST rebuild with dev or build --debug before reading the position ([DEV-182]). authoring-onboarding Read the statement and write one test that fails when it is violated.
CMP-000 The removal minor of a marked item MUST be released at least 90 days after the release date of the marking minor, in addition to the two-minor rule of [ABI-052], and the release gate MUST block a removal whose marking release is younger than that (proposed, owner to confirm). compat-deprecation-timeline Release gate reads the marking release date from the support matrix and the planned release date; a fixture with a marking release 60 days old and a removal in the current notes fails the gate naming the item.
CMP-022 check --against <host-version> and test --host-contract <host-version> MUST report package.api-unsupported and manifest.api-version with the same code and message that install stage 3 reports, when the manifest requires range or the built component lies outside the selected host window. check MUST report the refusal as an error finding and exit 3, and test MUST refuse before any case runs and exit 1. reference-plugin-cli Build a plugin whose requires range excludes one host version, run check --against and test --host-contract with that version, and assert that both report package.api-unsupported and manifest.api-version with the same code and message as install stage 3, that check reports them as error findings and exits 3, and that test refuses before any case runs and exits 1.
CMP-023 Each refusal cell MUST name the command that observes the refusal, either ilium plugin check --against <host-version> or ilium plugin test --host-contract <host-version>, and that command MUST exit with a non-zero status for the refusal. guide-backwards-compatibility-test-matrix Read each refusal row of the matrix and assert that it names ilium plugin check --against or ilium plugin test --host-contract, and that the named command exits non-zero for that refusal.
CMP-024 Each host and SDK release MUST publish a deprecation register, as a page of the manual and as a JSON file with the same content, listing every item deprecated at that release with its kind (sdk, cli, contract or unstable-feature), its successor, its removal minor and the release that marked it. compat-deprecation-timeline Check the latest release for a deprecation register page and a JSON file with the same items, each with a kind of sdk, cli, contract or unstable-feature, a successor, a removal minor and the release that marked it.
CMP-025 The register MUST drop an item only in the release that removes it, and the release notes of that release MUST name the item exactly as the register does. compat-deprecation-timeline Compare the register of a release that removes an item with the register of the release before it in a scratch copy, and assert that the item appears only in the earlier register and that the removing release's notes name it exactly as the register does.
PUB-000 A version in queued-review MUST carry review_queued_at (UTC, second precision) in its plugins/<id>.json entry and ilium plugin info <id>@<version> MUST print it; when the time since review_queued_at exceeds the review deadline stated in policy.json (5 working days, proposed, owner to confirm) the plugin page MUST show Review overdue and the version MUST stay at level A (proposed, owner to confirm). publish-publisher-workflow Publish a package that needs level B, read plugins/.json and info --json for review_queued_at; advance the registry clock past the deadline and check the plugin page text and that review_level stays A.
PUB-042 A review refusal of a queued-review version MUST be handled as a takedown of that version under [PKG-403] and [PKG-821] (blob removed, tombstone kept, registry.version-exists for a re-publish of the same id@version), MUST record the policy rule and a reason readable through ilium plugin info <id>@<version>, and MUST NOT move the version to rejected with a free version number, because clients may already have installed it at level A (proposed, owner to confirm). publish-publisher-workflow Queue a version, install it on a client at level A, then refuse the review; the client moves the copy to disabled-blocked at the next refresh, plugins/.json keeps the tombstone, and a publish of the same id@version is refused with registry.version-exists.
PUB-043 An appeal MUST NOT suspend the takedown. The blocked_ids entry MUST stay in revocations.json, and installed copies MUST stay disabled-blocked, until the decision is published. After a successful appeal the registry MUST remove an id-level blocked_ids entry so that the publisher can publish a new version under the rules of PKG-404, and it MUST keep every version tombstone of PKG-821 (proposed, owner to confirm). publish-registry-operator-guide Take down an id, file an appeal, refresh a client: the plugin stays disabled-blocked. Record the appeal as successful: revocations.json no longer lists the id, the tombstones remain in plugins/.json, and a publish of a new version succeeds.
PUB-044 The operator MUST accept an appeal only from a maintainer of the publisher id, authenticated by the registry account with its second factor or by a signature of a trusted key of that publisher id. An appeal from anyone else MUST be refused and MUST NOT use up the single appeal allowed by PKG-404. When the registry has more than one operator, the decision MUST be made by an operator who did not approve the takedown (proposed, owner to confirm). publish-registry-operator-guide Send an appeal from an account that is not a maintainer: it is refused and the maintainer's later appeal is still accepted. On a two-operator test registry, record the appeal decision under the same operator who approved the takedown: the registry refuses to log it.
PUB-045 The registry MUST NOT include the identity, address or report text of an abuse reporter in revocations.json, quarantine.json, policy.json, any transparency log entry, any plugin page, or any notice to the maintainers of the reported plugin. Only the operator's private record may hold them (proposed, owner to confirm). publish-registry-operator-guide File a report with a unique reporter address and unique report text, take the version down, then search every served document, the log entries and the maintainer notice for both strings; no match.
PUB-046 The abuse intake of PKG-705 MUST accept a report that names a plugin id, a version or a package sha256, and one rule id of policy.json. It MUST return a report id in the acknowledgement, and it MUST send the reporter the recorded decision (yank, takedown, quarantine, or none with a stated reason) with the index of its transparency log entry (proposed, owner to confirm). publish-registry-operator-guide Submit a report through the documented intake on a test registry; the acknowledgement arrives within 1 business day and carries a report id; after the decision the reporter receives the decision and the log entry index, and log/entries/.json has type abuse-decision.
PUB-047 The registry MUST refuse a yank reason, a deprecate message or a takedown reason that contains a control character other than line feed, with registry.reason-invalid; a client MUST render these texts as plain text, MUST NOT interpret them as links or terminal escapes, and MUST truncate them at 500 Unicode scalar values on screen (proposed, owner to confirm). publish-yank-deprecate-takedown Run ilium plugin yank with a reason containing an ESC byte: refused with registry.reason-invalid. Yank with a reason holding a URL and OSC-like text: ilium plugin info output contains no escape bytes and the text is not clickable.
PUB-048 After a takedown, the registry MUST send a notice to every maintainer of every plugin whose latest release has a non-optional requires.plugins range that only the taken-down version satisfies, and MUST record the count of such dependents in the takedown's transparency log entry (proposed, owner to confirm). publish-yank-deprecate-takedown Publish B requiring A exactly at 1.0.0, take down A@1.0.0, check the maintainers of B receive a notice and the takedown log entry carries dependents 1; take down a version with no dependents and check the count is 0.
PUB-049 During the 24-hour decision window of PKG-705 the operator MAY quarantine the reported range through quarantine.json. When the decision is none, the quarantine MUST be withdrawn (EXT-059) within 24 hours of that decision (proposed, owner to confirm). When the decision is a takedown, the quarantine entry MUST be withdrawn in the same metadata change that adds the blocked_ids entry (proposed, owner to confirm). publish-registry-operator-guide Quarantine a range after a report, record decision none, advance the clock 24 hours: quarantine.json carries a withdrawn entry for the range. Record a takedown instead: the snapshot that lists the new revocations.json also lists a quarantine.json with the range withdrawn.
PUB-050 A rights holder MUST send a claim that names the plugin id, the version or the package sha256, the work claimed, the proof of ownership, the legal name and a contact address of the rights holder, and a statement of good faith. A claim without one of these items MUST be answered with a request for the missing item, and it MUST NOT start the decision window of PUB-051 (proposed, owner to confirm). publish-rights-claims Send a claim without the proof of ownership and assert the reply names that item and no decision window starts; send a complete claim and assert its window starts at the acknowledgement.
PUB-051 The operator MUST acknowledge a complete claim within 1 business day with a claim id, and MUST decide within 10 business days whether to quarantine, take down or take no action. The decision MUST be sent to the claimant and to every maintainer of the publisher id (proposed, owner to confirm: 10 business days). publish-rights-claims File a complete claim, check the claim id and acknowledgement arrive within 1 business day, then check the decision reaches the claimant and every maintainer within 10 business days of the claim.
PUB-052 While a complete claim is open, the operator MAY quarantine the version the claim names through quarantine.json (EXT-057). The operator MUST NOT quarantine a version that the claim does not name. publish-rights-claims Quarantine one of two live versions of a test plugin and assert quarantine.json names only that version, the other version still resolves and an installed copy of the quarantined one keeps running.
PUB-053 A publisher whose version is quarantined or taken down for a claim MAY send a counter-notice to the claims address, stating the version, why the publisher believes the claim is wrong, and a contact address. The operator MUST forward the counter-notice to the claimant within 1 business day and MUST tell the publisher the time of forwarding (proposed, owner to confirm). publish-rights-claims Send a counter-notice for a quarantined version and assert the publisher receipt carries the time of forwarding and that it arrives within 1 business day.
PUB-054 When the claimant does not show a court filing or a written agreement within 14 calendar days of the forwarding of a counter-notice, the operator MUST withdraw the quarantine of that version within 1 business day. The operator MUST NOT reverse a takedown on the counter-notice alone; a taken-down version comes back only as a new version under PKG-404 (proposed, owner to confirm: 14 calendar days). publish-rights-claims With a test clock, advance 14 calendar days after forwarding with no claimant filing and assert the quarantine is withdrawn; repeat with a takedown and assert it stays disabled-blocked.
PUB-055 When three claims against one publisher id are upheld within 12 months, the operator MUST suspend that publisher id under PKG-091 for 90 days, and MUST tell every maintainer of the publisher id the number of upheld claims and the date of the last one (proposed, owner to confirm: three upheld claims within 12 months, 90 days). publish-rights-claims Record three upheld claims against one test publisher id within 12 months and assert the id is suspended for 90 days and every maintainer receives the count and the date of the last claim.
PUB-056 The registry MUST record every decision on a claim in the transparency log with the claim id, the plugin id, the version, the decision and the time. It MUST NOT publish the claimant's contact address, the text of a counter-notice or the identity of the person who filed the claim; those stay in the operator's private record (proposed, owner to confirm). publish-rights-claims After a decision, read the transparency log entry and assert it holds the claim id, plugin id, version, decision and time, and no claimant contact address or counter-notice text.
PUB-057 A release whose manifest license differs from the license of the previous version MUST name the old and the new SPDX identifier in its release notes, and ilium plugin info <id>@<version> MUST print both identifiers (proposed, owner to confirm). guide-publishing-and-support Publish a test release that changes license from MIT to Apache-2.0 with release notes that name only one identifier; assert the release is held, then with both named assert ilium plugin info prints both.
PUB-058 With auto_update = install, the host MUST NOT install a version whose license differs from the license of the installed version. It MUST show the change as a notice, and it MUST install the version only after the user runs ilium plugin update <id> (proposed, owner to confirm). guide-publishing-and-support Run a test host with auto_update = install against a test registry that publishes a version with a new license; assert the version is not installed, a notice appears, and it installs only after ilium plugin update <id>.
PUB-059 The registry MUST NOT change the license of a version entry after publish. A fork of an older version MUST keep the license that the forked version shipped with, and the registry MUST NOT treat a later licence change as a change to that version. guide-publishing-and-support Read the signed version entry of an old version before and after a release that changes the licence and assert the license value is byte-identical; fork the old version and assert the fork's manifest keeps the old identifier.
PUB-060 Before a release changes the licence of a plugin, the publisher MUST hold written consent from every contributor whose code is still in the tree of that release, or MUST remove or rewrite that code first. The release notes MUST say which of the two was done (proposed, owner to confirm). guide-publishing-and-support In a test repository with two contributors, prepare a licence-changing release with consent from only one and assert the release is held; with both consents or a removal recorded, assert the notes say which was done.
PUB-061 The registry operator MUST screen every new publisher account against the sanctions lists that bind the operator, at account creation and before the operator issues a new token to an existing account. The operator MUST refuse a match with registry.account-refused and MUST NOT issue a token to it (proposed, owner to confirm: the lists are named in policy.json). governance Create a test account whose name matches an entry of a fixture sanctions list and assert the reply is registry.account-refused with no token; repeat with a token request on an existing account.
PUB-062 A refusal on sanctions grounds MUST NOT name the list, the matched entry or the country to the requester. The requester MUST see only registry.account-refused and the claims contact of policy.json, so that the operator can answer a mistaken match (proposed, owner to confirm). governance Assert the refusal body contains only the code and the claims contact, and does not contain the list name, the matched entry or the country.
PUB-063 The operator MUST keep the screening result and the date of each screen in the operator's private record. The registry MUST NOT publish the result in revocations.json, policy.json, the transparency log or any plugin page (proposed, owner to confirm). governance Screen an account and assert the result is in the operator's private record fixture and does not appear in revocations.json, policy.json, the transparency log or the account's plugin page.
PUB-064 The project MUST keep a written export classification statement for every encryption function of the host, the WASM sandbox and the TLS client. The statement MUST name each library and each algorithm, MUST be updated in the same release as any change of a cryptographic dependency, and MUST be reviewed by counsel before a release that adds a cryptographic function (proposed, owner to confirm). governance Read the classification statement and check that each encryption function in the release SBOM has a row naming its library and algorithm; add a cryptographic dependency without a row and assert the release check fails.
PUB-065 A package that bundles a non-code asset, meaning a model weight file, a dataset, a font, an image or a sound file, MUST list each asset in its NOTICE file with the asset's path in the package, its source, its licence name or SPDX identifier, and its attribution text (proposed, owner to confirm). guide-publishing Pack a test plugin with one font and one model file, leave the font out of NOTICE, and assert the level B check fails with license-notice-missing; add the entry and assert the check passes.
PUB-066 An author MUST NOT package an asset whose licence does not allow redistribution in the package. The author MUST instead tell the user where to fetch that asset. A level B review MUST refuse a version that contains such an asset with registry.policy and the detail asset-licence-missing (proposed, owner to confirm). guide-publishing Package a test asset whose licence text forbids redistribution and assert pack warns, and a level B publish of it is refused with registry.policy and asset-licence-missing.
PUB-067 The manifest license MUST describe the plugin code only. The licence of each bundled asset is stated in NOTICE under PUB-065, and the registry MUST NOT treat the manifest license as the licence of an asset. guide-publishing Give a test plugin an MIT manifest license and a bundled non-commercial asset; assert ilium plugin info shows the MIT identifier as the plugin licence and the asset appears only in NOTICE.
PUB-068 A use restriction in an asset licence, such as a limit to non-commercial use or to a field of use, MUST appear in NOTICE in the words of the licence text, and the README MUST state the restriction in plain words. A level B review MUST check each listed asset against the package by its SHA-256 and MUST record the number of assets checked in the review record as assets_checked (proposed, owner to confirm). guide-publishing Change one byte of a listed asset after review and assert the review check fails the SHA-256 comparison; with the original bytes assert the review record has assets_checked equal to the number of listed assets.
PUB-069 A plugin MAY be sold, or licensed with a licence key, under any licence its author chooses. The registry MUST NOT refuse a publish because the plugin charges for use (proposed, owner to confirm). governance Publish a test plugin whose README states a price and a licence key check and assert the registry accepts the publish, with no refusal code in the reply.
PUB-070 A plugin that charges for use MUST carry its end-user terms in its LICENSE file or in a terms file named in its README, and MUST state in its README the price model and the refund address (proposed, owner to confirm). governance Publish a paid test plugin without a terms file and assert the check reports the missing terms file; add the file and the README statement and assert plugin info names the terms file.
PUB-071 The registry operator MUST NOT take payment, hold entitlement data or mediate a refund for a plugin. The plugin page of a paid plugin MUST show the seller's contact address, and that address is the place where refund and support requests go (proposed, owner to confirm). governance Read the registry data of a test instance and assert it has no payment or entitlement table; open a paid test plugin page and assert the seller contact address is shown.
PUB-072 A licence key MUST NOT appear in the package, in a test fixture or in the release notes. The seller issues the key outside Ilium, and a plugin that checks a key MUST declare that check in its manifest, as the registry rules for licence-key plugins require (proposed, owner to confirm). governance Search the package, its test fixtures and the release notes of a test paid plugin for the licence key string and assert none is found; assert the manifest declares the key check.
PUB-073 The registry operator MUST accept legal process only at the address that policy.json names in legal_contact, and MUST verify the authenticity of each order (the issuing body, the official channel and the case number) before it acts on the order. publish-legal-requests send an order to an address other than legal_contact, and send an order with a case number that the issuing body does not confirm; the operator takes no action on either, and its private record shows both as rejected.
PUB-074 The registry operator MUST disclose user or publisher data in response to legal process only when the process is valid under the law of the jurisdiction named in policy.json, MUST limit the disclosure to the scope of the process, and MUST record each request, its legal basis and its outcome in the operator's private record. publish-legal-requests send a valid order that asks for the contact address of one publisher account, and check that only that field is disclosed and that the private record holds the order, its legal basis and the outcome.
PUB-075 The registry operator MUST publish a transparency report at least once every 12 months that counts legal requests, takedowns by category and appeals, and MUST NOT name a requester or a publisher whose data was not disclosed. publish-legal-requests Read the latest transparency report and check that it was published within 12 months of the previous report, that it has a count for legal requests, takedowns by category and appeals, and that no requester and no publisher id appears in a row for data that was not disclosed.
PUB-076 When a publisher or the operator reports that a published blob contains a secret or personal data, the operator MUST take the version down under PKG-403 and remove the blob from serving within 24 hours of the report. The operator MUST keep the digest and the tombstone under PKG-821, and MUST record the reason and the time in the transparency log. publish-yank-deprecate-takedown plant a labelled synthetic token in a fixture blob, report it, and fetch the blob path; the fetch does not return the blob, plugins/<id>.json keeps the digest and a tombstone, and the transparency log has an entry with the reason and the time, made within 24 hours of the report.
PUB-077 The publisher MUST rotate the leaked secret before the operator reinstates any version with the same digest, and the release notes of the replacement version MUST state that the earlier version was withdrawn for a secret leak without repeating the secret. publish-yank-deprecate-takedown Report a secret leak for a fixture version, ask the operator to reinstate a version with the same digest before any rotation record exists and check that the reinstatement is refused; then check that the replacement version's release notes state that the earlier version was withdrawn for a secret leak and do not contain the secret string.
PUB-078 The registry operator MUST answer a written erasure request from a publisher account holder within 30 days, MUST erase the contact address, the display name and the recovery data of that account, and MUST keep the transparency log entries, which carry only key fingerprints and publisher ids. publish-registry-operator-guide Send an erasure request for a fixture account, complete it within 30 days, and check that the store holds no contact address, display name or recovery data for that account, and that its transparency log entries remain with only key fingerprints and publisher ids.
PUB-079 The registry operator MUST state in its private record the retention period of account data, of the access logs and of each backup, and MUST delete an erased account's data from every backup no later than the first restore cycle that follows the erasure request. publish-registry-operator-guide erase a fixture account, run one restore cycle from a backup taken before the request, and check that the restored store holds no data of that account except its transparency log entries.
PUB-080 The official registry operator MUST state a monthly availability objective of 99.5 percent for metadata and blob serving on the status page, and MUST post an outage notice on the status page within 1 hour of detecting an outage that lasts more than 15 minutes. publish-registry-operator-guide Read the status page and check that the monthly availability objective for metadata and blob serving is stated as 99.5 percent for each calendar month; then simulate a 20-minute outage of a fixture host and check that the outage notice is posted on the status page within 1 hour of detecting it.
PUB-081 During an outage the client MUST keep using its cached signed metadata and its installed packages, and MUST show the time of the last successful refresh in ilium plugin registry status. publish-registry-operator-guide block the registry host, run ilium plugin registry status and check that it prints the time of the last successful refresh; then run ilium plugin install of a version that is in the cache and check that it succeeds from the cache.
PUB-082 A level B review MUST be recorded by a reviewer who has completed the review training named in the operator's private record and who has declared to the operator no financial or personal link to the publisher, and a refusal MUST be confirmed by a second reviewer before it takes effect. publish-registry-operator-guide record a refusal as the first reviewer and check that the version keeps its previous state; record a level B review by a reviewer with no training record and check that it is refused; confirm a refusal with a second reviewer and check that it takes effect.
PUB-083 Each quarter the registry operator MUST re-review at least 5 percent of that quarter's level B decisions, rounded up to a whole decision, by a reviewer who was not involved in the original decision, and MUST state the agreement rate of those re-reviews in the transparency report. publish-registry-operator-guide at the end of a quarter, count the level B decisions and the re-reviews; check that the re-reviews are at least 5 percent of the decisions, rounded up, that each has a reviewer id different from the original reviewer, and that the transparency report states the agreement rate.
PUB-084 (proposed, owner to confirm) A version at any review level MUST carry a NOTICE entry, as [PUB-065] describes, for every bundled asset that is not code under the manifest license. This replaces the exemption of [PKG-682] for assets only: the SBOM and the licence notice stay optional at level A. The registry MUST refuse the publish with registry.policy and the detail asset-notice-missing when an asset has no entry. guide-publishing Publish a level A package that contains a font with no NOTICE entry for it and assert the refusal with registry.policy and the detail asset-notice-missing; add the entry and assert that the publish succeeds.
PUB-085 (proposed, owner to confirm) A plugin that bundles code of another plugin MUST carry the licence text of that plugin in its NOTICE. The registry MUST refuse a publish whose requires.plugins names a plugin whose license is listed in policy.json as incompatible with the license of the publishing plugin, with registry.policy and the detail licence-incompatible. guide-publishing List the licence of a sample plugin as incompatible with the licence of a second sample, publish the second plugin with a requires.plugins entry for the first and assert the refusal with registry.policy and the detail licence-incompatible; remove the listing and assert the publish succeeds.
OPS-000 The host MUST refuse an http request to a host named in the plugin's telemetry_hosts with not-permitted while the plugin's telemetry consent is not granted, MUST write the log line refused telemetry:<host> for it, and MUST NOT refuse requests to hosts outside that list on that ground (proposed, owner to confirm). ops-telemetry-consent With consent not-asked, request the declared telemetry host and an ordinary granted host from a fixture plugin; assert not-permitted and the log line for the first and success for the second; set granted and assert the first now succeeds.
OPS-012 The host MUST expose the telemetry consent state to the plugin as the read-only setting key telemetry.consent with the values not-asked, granted and declined, MUST deliver each change as a settings-changed event whose keys holds telemetry.consent, and MUST refuse a plugin write to that key with not-permitted (proposed, owner to confirm). ops-telemetry-consent Read the key from a fixture plugin in each of the three states; change the state and assert one settings-changed event naming the key arrives before the next call; attempt settings.set on the key and assert not-permitted.
OPS-013 When an update changes the plugin's [privacy] table (collects, retention_days or telemetry_hosts), the host MUST set the telemetry consent of a granted plugin back to not-asked, MUST write a consent-withdrawn audit record with the reason declaration-changed, and MUST show on the settings page that the plugin's privacy declaration changed (proposed, owner to confirm). ops-telemetry-consent Grant consent, update the plugin to a version that adds a collects entry, and assert the state is not-asked, one consent-withdrawn record with reason declaration-changed exists and the settings page shows the notice; update to a version with an unchanged table and assert the state stays granted.
OPS-014 The host MUST NOT set the telemetry consent of a plugin to granted when its manifest has no [privacy] table: the settings page MUST show the consent control disabled with the text 'This plugin does not describe what it collects', and the CLI MUST refuse with consent.no-privacy-declaration (proposed, owner to confirm). ops-telemetry-consent Install a plugin with telemetry_hosts but no collects, try to grant from the settings page and from the CLI, and assert the control is disabled with that text, the CLI exits non-zero with the code, and the state stays not-asked.
OPS-015 When an administrator policy blocks plugin telemetry, the plugin's settings page and the telemetry line of ilium plugin grants <plugin-id> MUST show blocked by policy beside the consent state, and the consent control MUST stay usable so that the user's own state is kept (proposed, owner to confirm). ops-telemetry-consent Set the policy to block telemetry, grant consent, and assert both views print granted and blocked by policy; remove the policy and restart the server and assert blocked by policy disappears and the state is still granted.
OPS-016 ilium plugin restore --include-grants and ilium plugin import-data MUST restore a telemetry consent as not-asked unless --include-consents is given, and every telemetry state that a restore or import changes MUST write the audit record of [OPS-104] with the actor restore or import (proposed, owner to confirm). ops-telemetry-consent Back up with a granted consent, erase, restore without the flag and assert not-asked and no record; restore with --include-consents and assert granted and one consent-given record with actor restore.
OPS-017 The host MUST create /tmp/.ilium-<uid>/ and its logs/<session-id>/ folders with mode 0700 owned by the running user and each log file with mode 0600, MUST NOT follow a symbolic link at any of those paths, and MUST refuse to write the diagnostics log, showing log directory not writable: <path> instead, when the root folder exists with another owner, with a wider mode or as a link (proposed, owner to confirm). Test: pre-create /tmp/.ilium-<uid> as a symlink to a scratch folder, enable file logging, and assert the notice, no file in the scratch folder and the server still running; then remove the link, re-enable and stat the created folders and file for 0700 and 0600. ops-diagnostics-and-logs Test: pre-create /tmp/.ilium-<uid> as a symlink to a scratch folder, enable file logging, and assert the notice, no file in the scratch folder and the server still running; then remove the link, re-enable and stat the created folders and file for 0700 and 0600.
OPS-018 A diagnostics log file MUST NOT grow past 64 MiB. When the cap is reached the host MUST write one final line [log cap reached, further lines dropped], MUST stop appending to that file for the rest of the server lifetime, MUST count the dropped lines, and MUST show the count in the diagnostics report (proposed, owner to confirm). Test: enable file logging, write lines until the file reaches the cap, and assert that the file ends with the marker line, that its size stays within 64 MiB plus one line after 1,000 more writes, and that the report shows the dropped count. ops-diagnostics-and-logs Test: enable file logging, write lines until the file reaches the cap, and assert that the file ends with the marker line, that its size stays within 64 MiB plus one line after 1,000 more writes, and that the report shows the dropped count.
OPS-226 The host MUST accept a diagnostics log folder inside the state folder, set with [diagnostics] log_dir in config.toml, and MUST use it in place of /tmp/.ilium-<uid>/logs when the key is set, with the modes of OPS-017. A path outside the state folder MUST be refused, the host MUST keep the default folder, and it MUST show a warning that names the key. ops-diagnostics-and-logs Set [diagnostics] log_dir to a folder inside the state folder, enable file logging, restart the server and assert that the new log file is written under that folder; then set log_dir to a path outside the state folder and assert that the host keeps the default folder and shows a warning that names the key log_dir.
OPS-227 When the server starts, the host MUST delete each diagnostics log file whose newest line is older than 30 days (proposed, owner to confirm), and MUST NOT delete the five newest files of the session. ops-diagnostics-and-logs Create seven log files whose newest lines are 31 days old, start the server, and assert that exactly two of them are removed and the five newest files of the session remain.
OPS-228 The host MUST write every line whose code starts with host. to <state>/host/host.log, whether or not diagnostics file logging is on, with mode 0600, and MUST keep at most four rotated files of 4 MiB each. ops-diagnostics-and-logs With file logging off, cause a loop stall and a disk-low step, and assert that both host. lines appear in <state>/host/host.log with mode 0600, and that rotation keeps at most four rotated files of 4 MiB each.
OPS-229 The host threshold for lines whose code starts with host. MUST default to info, MUST be set with [diagnostics] host_level, and a change MUST take effect without a restart, as OPS-002 requires for file logging. ops-diagnostics-and-logs set host_level to debug, cause a debug-level host line, and assert that it appears without a restart.
OPS-230 The project MUST publish a four-level severity scale for operational incidents, with an acknowledgement time and an owner for each level, as the table of this page sets them. ops-incident-response A tabletop review assigns one of the four severity levels to each of five fixture incidents, and the scale gives each of the four levels an owner and an acknowledgement time as the table of the page sets them.
OPS-231 While the server runs, the host MUST detect a change of the system policy file within 10 seconds of the change. For each running plugin that the new effective policy blocks through plugins.deny_ids, packages.allowed_tiers, packages.allow_third_party or a publisher rule, the host MUST deactivate every running instance of that plugin within the times of HST-517 after the detection, with the reason policy (proposed, owner to confirm). reference-admin-policy add a block entry to the file while a fixture plugin runs, and assert that the plugin is deactivated within 10 seconds plus the times of HST-517 (1 s on the server, 5 s on each attached client).
OPS-232 Each live reload that changes the effective policy MUST write one audit record policy-reloaded that holds the SHA-256 hash of the system policy file before the change and after it (proposed, owner to confirm). reference-admin-policy edit the file twice, reload after each edit, and assert two policy-reloaded records, each with the hash before and after its own edit.
OPS-233 ilium plugin health --json MUST print one JSON line per installed plugin with the fields id, version, side, state, reason and restarts_10m, and MUST keep the exit codes of HST-617. state is the health value of the first table, reason is the reason of its matching row or null, side is server or client when the matching row names a side and none otherwise, and restarts_10m is the number of restarts of the plugin's sides in the last 10 minutes, the window of LIF-134 (proposed, owner to confirm). reference-health-and-watchdog run the command with three fixture plugins in the states healthy, degraded and failed, and assert three JSON lines with those fields and exit code 2.
OPS-234 The --json output of ilium plugin health MUST contain no log text and no plugin data, MUST write the fields of OPS-233 in that order on every line, and MUST keep the field names and their order across releases within one ABI major version (proposed, owner to confirm). reference-health-and-watchdog produce the output for the same three fixture plugins with two releases, and assert identical field names and order, and that no line of the fixture logs appears in the output.
OPS-235 Every host crash record MUST contain the build id of the running server binary and the commit hash of its source. For host records these two fields extend the field list of [SEC-446], and the redaction test of SEC-446 still applies (proposed, owner to confirm). reference-audit-log force a host panic in a release build, read the record, and assert that the build id and the commit hash are present and that the redaction test passes.
OPS-236 Every release MUST publish the debug symbol files for the build id of each host binary it ships, next to SHA256SUMS, so that the frames of a host crash record can be resolved against that release (proposed, owner to confirm). reference-host-release-verification For a release, assert that a debug symbol file for the build id of each shipped host binary is published next to SHA256SUMS.
OPS-237 ilium plugin doctor MUST print the build id of the last host crash on the same line as the time of that crash (proposed, owner to confirm). user-safe-mode-and-troubleshooting force a host crash, run ilium plugin doctor, and assert that the build id is on the same line as the crash time.
OPS-238 build-report MUST write the report only to the path given with --out <file>, or, when no path is given, to <state>/reports/ with folder mode 0700 and file mode 0600. It MUST NOT write the report into a plugin data folder (proposed, owner to confirm). ops-diagnostics-and-logs Build a report without a path and assert that the <state>/reports/ folder has mode 0700 and the file has mode 0600; build a report with --out to a fresh path and assert that the file is written only at that path.
OPS-239 ilium plugin doctor MUST list each saved report older than 30 days (proposed, owner to confirm) with its path and size, and MUST NOT delete it. ops-diagnostics-and-logs create a report whose file time is 31 days old, run ilium plugin doctor, and assert that the report is listed with its path and size and that the file still exists.
OPS-240 The host MUST append one integrity record to a sidecar file named <log file>.manifest.jsonl, with mode 0600, after every 1,000 lines of a plugin log or a diagnostics log and at each rotation of that log. Each record holds the number of lines so far, the SHA-256 hash of the log file up to that line, and the time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss. ilium plugin logs --verify MUST print ok when every record matches the log. Otherwise it MUST print mismatch with the log file name and the line count of the first record whose hash does not match, and MUST exit with code 1 (proposed, owner to confirm). ops-diagnostics-and-logs Write 2,500 lines to one log file, change one line between lines 1,001 and 2,000, and assert that ilium plugin logs --verify prints mismatch with the log file name and the line count 2000 and exits with code 1.
OPS-241 A manifest record MUST NOT contain log text or any other field of a log line (proposed, owner to confirm). ops-diagnostics-and-logs write a fixture secret into a plugin log, read the manifest, and assert that the secret is absent.
ACC-000 The host MUST draw an on-hover decoration on the session-tree row that holds keyboard focus as well as on the row under the pointer, and a plugin MUST NOT carry information only in an on-hover decoration. (proposed, owner to confirm) api-tree-chrome Fixture plugin sets a decoration with visibility: on-hover; move tree focus to that row with keys only and assert the decoration text is present in the screen text; move focus away and assert it is gone.
ACC-023 In linear mode the host MUST read each cell of a table row as <column title>: <cell text>, in column order, before the role word and the position. A plugin MUST give every table column a non-empty title. (proposed, owner to confirm) a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text Render a 3-column table with screen reader mode on and assert the row line holds each column title before its cell value; a column with an empty title must fail the view validator with ui.label-missing naming the column id.
ACC-024 In linear mode the host MUST print the title of a block or panel on its own line, before the first element inside it. A plugin MUST give a non-empty title to every block that contains a focusable widget. (proposed, owner to confirm) a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text Render a view with two titled blocks of two buttons each in screen reader mode; assert the output has the block titles as lines immediately before their buttons; a block with focusable children and no title fails ilium plugin lint with a named finding.
ACC-025 In linear mode the host MUST print non-focusable text widgets (paragraph, markdown, notice, leader-row, badge and key-hints) as plain lines in tree order, between the focusable lines. It MUST read a gauge, line-gauge, meter or progress-row as its label followed by its percentage as digits and the word percent. (proposed, owner to confirm) a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text Render a view with a notice, a gauge at 0.37 and a button in screen reader mode; assert the notice text appears before the button line and the gauge line ends with 37 percent; no █ or ░ cell appears.
ACC-026 In linear mode the host MUST read a tree-list row with its depth as level <N>. For an expandable item it MUST also read the word expanded or collapsed after the position. (proposed, owner to confirm) a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text Render a tree-list with a collapsed parent at level 1 and a leaf at level 2 in screen reader mode; assert the lines end with 1 of 2, level 1, collapsed and level 2; expand with Right and assert expanded.
ACC-027 In linear mode the host MUST read a secret text-input as filled or empty, and MUST NOT print any character of its value. A plugin MUST NOT copy a secret value into a label, a status row or a tooltip. (proposed, owner to confirm) a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text Render a secret text-input holding hunter2 in screen reader mode and assert the line is <label>, text field, filled and the screen text contains no h,u,n sequence; lint flags a tooltip or label built from a secret-field value.
ACC-028 After a re-render that keeps the focused element, the host MUST keep the cursor on the first cell of that element in linear mode. It MUST NOT move the cursor to the first line of the view. (proposed, owner to confirm) a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text Focus the third element in screen reader mode, trigger invalidate with an unchanged tree, and assert the harness cursor position equals the first cell of the same element; repeat with one row added above it and assert the cursor followed the element.
ACC-029 When a popup, dialog or panel opens without a focus request, the host MUST place focus on the first focusable node of its focus order, and a plugin MUST NOT require a click to put focus into a view it opened (proposed, owner to confirm). a11y-keyboard-and-focus Open a panel and a popup with keys only in the fake host and assert focused_key is the first node of the focus order; open a view with no focusable node and assert focus is unchanged and no action was sent.
ACC-030 When focus moves to a node inside a scroll-view, a scrollable paragraph, a %list, table or tree-list, the host MUST scroll that container so the focused node is fully visible before the next frame is drawn (proposed, owner to confirm). a11y-keyboard-and-focus Render a scroll-view of 30 buttons at 12 rows, Tab to the 20th button, and assert its label is on screen and the scrolled action reported the new offset; Shift+Tab back to the first and assert it is visible again.
ACC-031 A plugin MUST give every spinner a non-empty label. In linear mode the host MUST read a spinner as its label followed by the word busy, and the view validator MUST refuse a spinner without a label with ui.label-missing. (proposed, owner to confirm) a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text Render a spinner labelled Indexing in screen reader mode and assert the line Indexing, busy with no Braille frame glyph; render a spinner with no label and assert ui.label-missing.
ACC-032 A plugin that shows or hides content on hover-enter and hover-leave MUST show and hide the same content on focus-gained and focus-lost of the same node (proposed, owner to confirm). a11y-keyboard-and-focus Fixture view reveals a preview row on hover; drive focus-gained on the node with Tab and assert the preview row is in the screen text, Tab away and assert it is gone; the same test with a pointer hover must produce the same tree.
ACC-033 When [ui] screen_reader changes while plugin views are open, the host MUST render every open plugin view again in the new mode within one frame and MUST deliver theme-changed, so that a plugin needs no code and no restart to switch modes. (proposed, owner to confirm) a11y-screen-reader-and-localized-text Open a plugin view, flip ui.screen_reader in the test host settings, assert the next screen text is in linear form without a plugin render call being required, and assert exactly one theme-changed event reached the plugin.
ACC-034 A plugin MUST NOT close a dialog that awaits a decision, activate one of its buttons or change its default button on a timer; such a dialog MUST close only on a user action or when the subject it asks about no longer exists, and then with closed, never with an activated the user did not send (proposed, owner to confirm). a11y-keyboard-and-focus Open the plugin's confirm dialog in the fake host, advance the fake clock by 120 s with no input, and assert the dialog is still open, no activated was sent and the default button is unchanged.
ACC-035 A plugin MUST NOT bind F1, Shift+F10 or the Menu key to a command, a keybinding or a key capture of its own, and MUST NOT capture the drag mark chord of the active keymap preset (Ctrl+Space for tmux, m for screen) while a draggable node has focus; the host keeps these keys for the tooltip, the context menu and the keyboard drag (proposed, owner to confirm). a11y-keyboard-and-focus ilium plugin lint fails a manifest whose keybindings use F1, Shift+F10 or Menu; in the fake host, press F1 on a focused node with a tooltip and Shift+F10 on a keyed node and assert the tooltip appears and context-requested arrives, not a plugin command.
ONB-000 The first ilium plugin dev run of a fresh project MUST, within 10 s of a successful build, show the tree footer notice <name> (dev) is running. Press Ctrl+B then : to open Settings > Plugins. and the author MUST see the dev badge on the plugin row. When no session is reachable, the command MUST fail with session.unreachable and the hint MUST name the project folder in which to start ilium (proposed, owner to confirm). getting-started-first-plugin Create a project with plugin new, start an isolated ilium in it, run ilium plugin dev --json, assert the reload record, the footer notice text in the client capture, and the dev badge row; run dev again with no session and assert code session.unreachable, exit 6 and a hint that contains the project path.
